The Spanish hotel chain Meliá said Tuesday it will completely shutter its operations in Cuba, dealing a blow to the tourism industry on the Caribbean island grappling with strict sanctions and an energy blockade imposed by the United States.

A statement from the company said the decision, which will go into effect on Friday, was sue to “the significant operational, legal, economic and financial difficulties that have persistently affected, and continue to affect, the environment" in Cuba.

Cuba's tourism industry was formerly an engine of the country's economy. Meliá's decision follows new sanctions announced by the U.S. on July 13 blacklisting Cuba’s Ministry of Tourism, the business partner of more than a dozen hotels that the hotel chain still operated on the island.

The chain had previously suspended management of 15 hotels it operated through an agreement with a tourism agency run by GAESA, a Cuban military-business conglomerate that was sanctioned by the U.S. in May. The company has now completely withdrawn its business from Cuba.

Meliá once owned 34 five-star hotels in Cuba, primarily in Havana, the country's capital, and idyllic locations such as the Varadero resort and the main keys. It was also a highly symbolic chain for the island, following the opening of tourism in the Caribbean nation after the collapse of the Soviet Union more than 35 years ago.

U.S. measures against companies operating in Cuba include freezing their assets and seizing their accounts in the U.S. — meaning they can no longer operate in the U.S. financial market — and also travel bans for their shareholders, investors and employees.

The U.S. ramped up pressure on the island following the capture of Venezuela's then-President Nicolás Maduro in January, seeking the fall of the Cuban government and changes to its political and economic model. It also implemented an energy embargo that has exacerbated a pre-existing crisis.

The result has been daily blackouts lasting more than 20 hours, medicine shortages pushing the healthcare system to the brink, a collapsed water supply and paralyzed transportation.

Meliá’s departure demonstrates the resounding impact of U.S. President Donald Trump’s policies, which are “methodically and systematically closing every source of foreign currency for the Cuban government,” Paolo Spadoni, an associate professor in the Department of Social Sciences at Augusta University in Georgia, told The Associated Press.

Tourism has plummeted with the withdrawal of major chains — such as the Spanish Iberostar and the Canadian Royalton — as well as the cancellation of flights to Cuba by airlines like World2Fly, Air France and Iberia.

This year, tourism arrivals in Cuba are down 48% compared to the same period in 2015, totaling just 298,000.

ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Tuesday that its artificial intelligence system hacked into another AI company on its own in what the company called an “unprecedented cyber incident.”

“We had a significant security incident during evaluation of our models,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a statement posted on social media.

AI startup Hugging Face said last week that it had detected an intrusion into its data processing systems that it suspected was caused by an AI agent autonomously acting on its own.

“We suspected last week’s cyberattack might have come from a frontier lab, given the sophistication of the agent,” Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clément Delangue said in a statement. "Turns out it did!”

The disclosure comes amid heightened concerns about the cybersecurity capabilities of powerful models that led President Donald Trump in June to sign an executive order creating a framework for the federal government to vet the national security risks of the most advanced AI systems for up to a month before their public release.

“AI is accelerating the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities,” OpenAI said in its statement Tuesday. “The primary lesson from this incident is that model security and safety must keep pace with rapidly advancing capabilities.”

Delangue said he spent the past 24 hours working with OpenAI, “and we strongly believe there was no malicious intent on their part. It’s quite mind-blowing that all of this happened autonomously!"

Delangue added that it “might be the first incident of its kind.”

OpenAI said the intrusion was caused by a combination of its AI models, including its newly released GPT‑5.6 Sol and an “even more capable” model that is still being tested internally.

OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face servers.

It went to “extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal” and “found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation,” the company said.

Millie Bobby Brown has led the tributes for her late co-star Kaylee Hottle, who has died at the age of 18.

The pair starred together in 2021’s Godzilla Vs Kong and its sequel, 2024’s Godzilla X Kong: The New Empire.

Hottle died as a result of a car crash that occurred in Maryland.

In response to the news, Brown wrote on Instagram: “I’m so devastated to hear this. You will be deeply missed Kaylee.”

In Godzilla vs Kong, Kaylee, who was deaf, portrayed Jia, a teenager who communicates with King Kong via sign language and lives on Skull Island with Rebecca Hall's character Dr. Ilene Andrews.

open image in gallery Millie Bobby Brown and Kaylee Hottle starred together in 2021's 'Godzilla Vs Kong' and its 2024 sequel ( Getty )

Her death was announced by her father, Joshua Hottle, who told TMZ of the news after posting a tearful Facebook livestream.

In the video, he explained in ASL that he was in Texas when he got a call from authorities about the collision, and that he received a follow-up call stating his daughter’s heart had stopped while on the way to the hospital.

Among the many paying tribute to Hottle was Marlee Matlin, the first deaf actress to win an Oscar. Matlin shared a photo on X with Hottle and fellow actress Shoshannah Stern, stating: "I am absolutely gutted about the passing of sweet Kaylee Hottle. May her beauty and talent be a memory for eternity."

Stern also posted about Hottle’s death on social media, writing: "I am heartbroken. My deepest sympathies to the Hottle family."

open image in gallery Kaylee Hottle in 2021's 'Godzilla Vs. Kong' ( PA )

Hottle, from Atlanta, Georgia, began her acting career in commercials. At nine, she starred in an ad for the live video messaging app Glide, which is used by many members of the deaf and hard-of-hearing community.

She also had a small role in the Prime Video action series Magnum P.I.

She was born in 2007 and, according to a 2024 interview with Chron magazine, she was scouted by casting director Sarah Halley Finn for the Godzilla role after appearing in an advert for the video relay service app Convo.

She also spoke about representation for deaf actors in Hollywood, saying: “I see a lot of positive things. There's not a lot of deaf roles or opportunities out there. And so now we're able, [and] I’m able to get them, and I think I've seen more and more growth and positivity.”

Hottle’s family spans four generations of deaf relatives on her father’s side.

In his Facebook post, Hottle’s father said that he was flying to Maryland to claim her body. He captioned the post: “I am taking a flight that I never would like to take.”

Venezuela confirmed on Tuesday that three people died of infections of hantavirus, but stressed there was no evidence of human-to-human transmission in the South American country, which has rarely reported cases of the rodent-borne disease in humans.

The Health Ministry said hantavirus was also suspected in the deaths of two health workers in the southwestern state of Barinas. Those cases remain under investigation and were not linked to the three fatalities in the eastern state of Anzoátegui, about 655 kilometers (407 miles) away.

Both states were spared the worst of the back-to-back major earthquakes that hit northern Venezuela earlier this month.

The ministry described the deaths in Anzoátegui and Barinas as isolated incidents that “do not represent a risk to the general community." But it added that health workers would be sent to the affected states to “guarantee the health security of all Venezuelans,” without elaborating.

The Venezuelan Medical Federation, a national professional group, said the deaths in Anzoátegui were from the same family in the rural municipality of Miranda in the south of the state.

Hantaviruses exist throughout the world and are spread mainly by contact with rodents such as rats and mice. It’s rare and not easy for a hantavirus to spread between people. In severe cases, the virus can cause a deadly lung infection or kidney failure.

As a recent deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic showed, some hantaviruses can spread between people in rare cases. The little-studied Andes hantavirus, detected in the outbreak that killed three passengers and infected several others on the MV Hondius in May, raised concerns around the world due to its mortality rate, as high as 30%, and the current lack of treatment and vaccines.

Weeks later in Argentina, from where the hantavirus-stricken cruise set sail, authorities are still trying to figure out the origin of the outbreak.

An early hypothesis circulated by officials suggested that patient zero, a Dutch ornithologist, may have become infected in the southernmost city of Ushuaia, famed for its location “at the end of the world." But Argentine scientists who tested rats for the Andes hantavirus in the area recently ruled out Ushuaia as the source of the outbreak — to the relief of the Antarctic cruise hub heavily reliant on foreign tourism.

Argentina also concluded the wine-producing province of Mendoza was not the source of contagion earlier this month, after local investigators and biologists from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention found no trace of hantavirus in rodents collected from areas visited by the Dutch man and his wife.

An attorney for the family of Nolan Xavier Wells says he will release the results of an independent autopsy into the 18-year-old’s death on Wednesday morning.

The preliminary findings are set to be made public during a news conference held at the annual NAACP National Convention in Chicago, according to the civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the family. Wells’ parents are expected to attend.

Crump has vowed to conduct his own investigation into the circumstances of the teenager's disappearance, which followed a July 4 boat trip with friends to an island off the coast of Mississippi. Wells did not return to the mainland with his friends. His body was found floating off the island’s coast two days later.

The Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office conducted its own autopsy but has yet to release the results.

The second autopsy was arranged by the family and Crump, and paid for by former NFL player Colin Kaepernick. Crump said it would determine if Wells “had any physical injuries to his body beyond drowning.”

The still-unknown circumstances around Wells’ death have touched off rampant online speculation and prompted calls from Black leaders for transparency from local authorities. Wells, who was Black, had traveled to the island with a group of high school friends, all of whom are white.

A reward of $125,000 — jointly funded by the Rev. Al Sharpton, actor and producer Tyler Perry and former NFL player Terrell Owens — is now being offered in exchange for information leading to an arrest and conviction in connection with the death.

The autopsy announcement comes two days after Wells was laid to rest in his hometown of Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

In his eulogy, Sharpton lamented the “inconsistencies and unanswered questions” that had placed a dark cloud over the grieving family.

He questioned why Wells’ friends had left him behind, taken his phone and keys and failed to report him missing to police. And he suggested local investigators had spoken prematurely in statements to the press indicating that no crime was suspected.

“The reason that a lot of people across the nation are looking at this Nolan situation is because we’re looking at the history in Mississippi,” Sharpton added. “We can’t have someone in law enforcement saying there was no foul play before there was an investigation.”

Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter said initial interviews suggested Wells chose to stay on the island and that his friends believed he would get a ride with someone else. He has said the friends were cooperating with the investigation, which remains ongoing.

“We are trying to be respectful and collaborative as much as we can,” Crump said. “But it’s always troublesome to all of us when these investigations just take forever.”

Taylor Farms, the produce company that voluntarily recalled its lettuce amid the ongoing diarrhea parasite outbreak, has spent recent years donating millions of dollars to groups aligned with President Trump and the Republican Party’s agenda.

Now, however, with more than 10,000 cases of cyclosporiasis logged across the U.S., the company is publicly battling and privately lobbying the White House.

Taylor Farms, which on Friday voluntarily recalled iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico, has given prolifically to support the GOP, according to a WIRED analysis of federal filings.

The spending spree has reportedly included giving more than $2 million to conservative groups in 2025, including $1 million to MAGA Inc., a Trump-aligned political action committee, as well as more than $1.6 million to conservative groups between 2020 and 2024, including $850,000 to an anti-regulation PAC tied to the Koch brothers network.

Bruce Taylor, chairman and CEO of the company, has also donated nearly $1 million to Republican PACs and candidates since 2020, WIRED found.

open image in gallery Taylor Farms and its CEO have given millions of dollars to support the Republican agenda, but the company recently disputed the Trump administration’s communications around the cyclosporiasis outbreak ( Getty )

All that reported support hasn’t necessarily smoothed things between the company and the administration.

“Nothing influences our decisions except science and the safety of the American people,” the Department of Health and Human Services wrote on X in a recent post, amid online speculation past support from Taylor Farms was swaying the Trump administration’s approach to the outbreak.

On Saturday, the Food and Drug Administration reported a sample of lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico tested positive for the diarrhea-causing parasite, only to later backtrack and declare the test a “false positive,” citing “the complexity in detection of Cyclospora.”

“FDA and state partners continue to collect and analyze product samples,” according to a current notice on the FDA website. “As of July 19, 2026, there are no confirmed positive sample results for product testing for Cyclospora.”

On Sunday, Taylor Farms wrote in a statement that “FDA apologized to us,” though an agency official soon told reporters it had not in fact given an “official apology” and was instead “providing factual information" about the status of the outbreak.

open image in gallery Late last week, the FDA walked back a claim that a sample of lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico tested positive for the diarrhea-causing parasite, calling that initial result a ‘false positive’ ( AFP/Getty )

The Independent has contacted the White House, Taylor Farms and the FDA for comment.

Last week, the company told The New York Times it had met with officials at the White House and FDA to discuss what it called “shortfalls in the F.D.A. and C.D.C.’s outbreak response process.”

Further White House contacts may be aided by a reported addition to Taylor’s lobbying team: Trent Morse, the former deputy director of the White House Presidential Personnel Office, who left the administration last year.

The lettuce company isn’t the only one taking issue with the Trump administration’s claims about the outbreak.

Mexico's Health Minister David Kershenobich said on Tuesday that there is no evidence to suggest lettuce from his country is the cause of the cyclosporiasis outbreak.

Critics argue the Trump administration’s DOGE cost-cutting program, which slashed federal agencies and pushed thousands of experienced federal workers to accept early retirements, has hamstrung the government’s ability to inspect produce for pathogens.

“The cuts across food safety, in terms of public health, in terms of regulatory, in terms of research, have contributed to this,” Barbara Kowalcyk, director of the Institute for Food Safety and Nutrition Security at George Washington University, recently told The New York Times. “I don’t think it’s a direct cause, but it’s been a contributing factor.”

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: The best cat food, recommended by a vet – including new online cat food delivery services
News.content:
As a cat carer for over 50 years and a vet for nearly 40, I understand the importance of finding the best cat food. It isn’t always easy to get it right. Cats need a complete and balanced diet providing protein, carbohydrate, fats, minerals, vitamins and fibre, as well as some specific nutrients such as taurine and essential fatty acids.

With such a huge range of products available, selecting the right one can be a real challenge. The aim of this article is to offer guidance on how to select the optimal diet for your feline friend. You can read my full reviews of the current best cat foods further down, followed by a comprehensive guide to cat nutrition, where you’ll learn how much and how often to feed your cat, among other things. But if you’re in a hurry, here’s a quick look at my top five:

The best cat foods: At a glance

Are cat food delivery services better than shopping in pet stores?

There are pros and cons to both. Online cat food delivery services such as Untamed, Republic of Cats and Katkin are new options and have the advantages of a wide variety of choice, combined with the convenience of delivery to your door. I write about some of them below. However, pet stores may have a wider choice and, in a physical store, you can pick and choose from products in front of you with expert advice.

How I chose the best cat foods

There are hundreds of different types and brands of cat food on the market: the following recommendations are based on my own experiences as a vet, plus feedback from the many cat owners to whom I talk.

Most brands tailor to different life stages – kitten, adult and senior – but only a few tailor to specific breeds, which is where my top choice Royal Canin really shines. Not all cat foods cater for special conditions, such as sensitive stomachs, so that was a factor in my choices too. I don’t need to tell you how fussy cats can be about their food.

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

Sports.title: What World Cup 2030 could look like with 64 teams as Gianni Infantino told to step down over insulting plans
Sports.content:
PICTURE the scene — it is prime time Saturday and the World Cup is on the box.

San Marino are taking on Angola in a group opener, while the rest of the weekend’s schedule includes Luxembourg v Kazakhstan and Faroe Islands v Libya.



Welcome to Gianni Infantino’s brave new world.

The Fifa president has been accused of systematically destroying football – and his latest brainwave is his most absurd yet.



Not content with watering down this summer’s tournament with 48 teams, Infantino is now plotting to expand the 2030 World Cup to a monstrous SIXTY-FOUR countries.

It is an insult to the beautiful game. This would mean almost one in three Fifa member nations will get a pass to the biggest show on Earth.

We will be forced to watch endless, meaningless group games while Fifa counts its broadcasting billions.

Though I suppose there is one silver lining — at least four-time champions Italy might finally qualify without suffering another humiliating play-off defeat against North Macedonia.

Make no mistake, Infantino does not care about the quality of football.

His endless expansion is not about growing the global game — it is a shameless vote-buying machine designed to keep him sitting on his Fifa throne until the end of time.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

As LaLiga chief Javier Tebas warned, Fifa is destroying the entire football ecosystem for a 40-day circus.

A 64-team World Cup means an absurd 128 MATCHES dragged out over six gruelling weeks. Player welfare? Don’t make me laugh.

Elite stars will be expected to run themselves into the ground playing up to 60 games for their clubs before flying across continents for a slog of group fixtures.

We already saw the warning signs this summer when Haiti, Tunisia, Iraq, Jordan, Uzbekistan and Panama all finished without a single point.

Curacao and Qatar barely fared better.



If a country wants to play on the grandest stage, there is already a perfectly fair mechanism to get here — it’s called qualifying.

Earn it on the pitch, lads.

But with 64 nations, can you imagine how many more meaningless qualifiers will be created, too?

And do not rule out the possibility of introducing fifth and seventh-place play-offs.

It sounds crazy but the way Infantino is going, anything considered ridiculous cannot be ruled out.



The leadership at the top is rotten. Infantino’s ten-year reign has become a masterclass in shameless bootlicking and corporate pandering.

Look at the utter joke of the 2030 scheduling already. Three opening matches are being staged in South America: Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina.

It will mark 100 years since they participated in the first competition held in Uruguay. This is before dragging teams across the Atlantic to Portugal, Spain and Morocco. All SIX automatically qualify as co-hosts, too.

Meanwhile, England — the actual home of football — have not hosted the tournament since winning it 1966.

At this rate, we will be waiting until 2066 for a measly ‘celebration game’.



And who could forget Infantino’s cringe-inducing brown-nosing?

Denied a Nobel Prize, Donald Trump was magically handed a newly manufactured ‘Fifa World Peace Prize’ by Infantino.

It was an embarrassing stunt to ingratiate himself with USA’s President.

Add to that the grotesque Americanisation of the matches.

Hydration breaks in air-conditioned stadiums as a shameless excuse for TV ad breaks and a ridiculous 27-minute half-time interval in the final to have Super Bowl-style entertainment with Madonna, Shakira and Ted Lasso.



Football became the biggest sport on Earth because it is fast, furious and continuous.

The Americans have always wanted to chop it into quarters and clog it up with commercials, but the World Cup final has always been bigger than the Super Bowl.

I’d love a return to 16 teams with guaranteed groups of death where every single game matters.

However, I accept 32 teams as a compromise between quality and being more inclusive. But Infantino has to go.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And if Fifa won’t stop him, European heavyweights like England, France, Spain, Germany and, yes, even Italy must step up and BOYCOTT the tournament.

Without the elite nations from Europe, Infantino’s bloated 64- team circus is meaningless.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr makes first public appearance after CHIN surgery as he packs on PDA with girlfriend after reigniting romance
Sports.content:
VINICIUS JR showed off the results of his chin surgery as he snogged his on-off influencer girlfriend.

The Real Madrid star, 26, is reported to have gone under the knife for the cosmetic procedure after Brazil’s World Cup exit.



And he showed off the results in his first public appearance since at the opening of Virginia Fonseca’s gym in Goiania.

The pair shared a smooch as Virginia posted: “Another dream come true!! Our @wegym_br 💜 thank you to everyone who came to support us on this special day and I hope you all from Goiania will train with us.”



Brazilian outlet TMC reported Vini Jr underwent a chin harmonisation procedure in Goiania after the tournament, which saw Brazil lose 2-1 to Norway in the last 16.

In a photo with dermatologist Dr Alessandro Alarcao, Vinicius’ chin was visibly different and more defined compared to before.



While there is no set cost for the cost of such a procedure, in the UK it can range anywhere from £3,000 to more than £14,000 depending on the treatment.

His new look comes as he confirmed his relationship with Virginia was back on.

She announced their split before the World Cup, after dating on and off since first being linked in 2025.

But they appeared to be very much back on when they were pictured on a superyacht together this month.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Vini Jr sparked outrage back home after snaps of the bikini-clad influencer sitting on his lap came out days after Brazil’s exit.

The Los Blancos star scored four times in the USA but did not net in the knockouts as Brazil were humbled by Erling Haaland.

He also copped flak for not stepping up to take the penalty against Norway, which Newcastle’s Bruno Guimaraes missed while the game was still 0-0.

And there was more fury when just ONE of Carlo Ancelotti’s squad flew home to Brazil to face the music.

Sports.title: Inside Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers’ bromance as they’re reunited – and Chelsea star’s role in £117m transfer revealed
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER will no longer have to reach for his phone to congratulate Morgan Rogers.

The Chelsea star, 24, has always been the first one to message his old pal whenever Rogers has scored or impressed in a game.



Now, the two former Manchester City academy team-mates are reunited at Stamford Bridge following a British record £117million deal struck by Chelsea for Rogers.

Whenever the ex-Villa man has had a good game he knows there will be a text waiting from Palmer when he gets into the dressing room.



The attacker told Goal last year: “Even after every game, he’s the first person to text me, or he’ll text me if I’ve scored, knowing I’ll see it after the game.

“It’s nice to have someone, with him doing well, checking up on you and whatnot.”

Despite their very close relationship, Chelsea did not ask Palmer to get in touch with Rogers and try to sway him towards signing after long-term interest from Arsenal.

Instead, it was new manager Xabi Alonso who led the charm offensive to scupper Gunners’ hopes of landing their priority target this summer.

The pair will certainly know how to celebrate if things go well under Alonso, too.

Palmer has made his shivering ‘ice cold’ celebration iconic since leaving Manchester City for the bright lights of west London, so much so that he has trademarked the term ‘Cold Palmer’.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But it was Rogers, who played with Palmer through the City academy and from England Under-15s to the senior squad, who did it first.

The new Chelsea man, who will turn 24 on Sunday, first displayed the shivering cold celebration after scoring for his former club Middlesbrough against West Brom in December 2023.

Days later Palmer notched a brace for the Blues against Luton and followed suit.

After the game, he said: “My boy Morgz did one for Middlesbrough, so told him I’d do it too, if I scored.

“It symbolises joy, passion and hard determination for the game, plus it’s funny as it works well with my name. Everyone knows it’s my celebration.



Lots of people might have done it, but everybody knows it is my celebration.”

Rogers then shot back: “He definitely copied me. It’s my celebration. Check the timeline, I did it first!”

The two had thought up the celebration during their days at City, but both had to leave the club in order to get regular game time.



However, they have only found entertainment from how the celebration debate has grown, though Rogers does concede it is probably more Palmer’s thing now.

The lad from Halesowen in the West Midlands added: “It’s funny how such a light-hearted conversation we had has turned into this now, and every interview he gets asked about me, and I get asked about him.

“It’s funny how it’s come that way and come that far, but to the world it’s probably more his thing than mine.”



The celebration may be synonymous with Palmer after his explosion at Chelsea, but if he cannot rediscover his form then we may be seeing far more of it from Rogers.

Chelsea’s new recruit scored 14 goals last term, including one in Villa’s Europa League final triumph, and registered 11 assists.

Palmer managed 11 goals and just three assists across an injury-hit season which saw him miss out on a World Cup place.

Rogers was one of those to go in his place, before darting down to London to complete his Chelsea medical as soon as England had returned from North America.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It will still be a few weeks before the two are properly reunited.



Palmer is heading Down Under and to the Far East on Chelsea’s pre-season tour while Rogers will have a well-earned break before linking up with the squad on their return.

Sports.title: Wayne and Coleen Rooney’s son Cass, 8, lands first modelling gig as he follows mum into fashion world
Sports.content:
WAYNE and Coleen Rooney’s youngest son emerges from the dressing room to kick off his modelling career — aged eight.

Cass Rooney made his debut alongside his mum to show off her latest collection of clothes for retailer Primark.



Coleen, 40, who has four sons with football pundit Wayne, said: “Having Cass as part of the kids­wear photoshoot was special.”

The Sun revealed in February she had signed a seven-figure deal with the high-street chain.



Her new collection launches next Tuesday, with her kidswear pieces available from next month.



She chose to stick to her budget roots and signed a contract with the affordable brand last year.

The move now cements Coleen as the Rooney family’s biggest breadwinner, with her sum beating out the £800,000 Wayne got last year to be a Match of the Day pundit at the BBC.

A source said at the time: “Coleen is so proud to be a working mum and she wanted to keep things affordable for her fans.



“She didn’t just sign for the cash, it was because she felt aligned with Primark’s values.

“Coleen is super proud with the clothes she’s worked on with Primark. It’s got a real athleisure feel. Primark thinks it will fly off the shelves.”

Another insider said: “Coleen is a perfectionist and throws herself into every project she gets involved in.

“With Primark, she worked so closely with them on the entire collection.

“It’s made for working mums just like her — the range is stylish yet practical.”



Coleen, 39, has previously signed big-money deals with George at Asda and Littlewoods — where she had her own collection for seven years.

Sports.title: Arteta suffers major injury headache as Arsenal stars clock up second most minutes at World Cup – how rivals compare
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA suffered more than a few gut punches watching his Arsenal stars at the World Cup.

So it was only fitting that the tournament ended with Mikel Merino sporting a juicy shiner under his eye.



Arsenal players arrived in the US running on fumes, and many have left looking like the walking wounded.

No more so is that the case than with Declan Rice, whose gruelling season is finally over.



The midfielder ended up playing 5,482 minutes across 69 games for club and country.

If anyone needs a holiday, it is Rice — but he is not alone.

Bukayo Saka has been troubled by an Achilles issue for months, while William Saliba’s back injury may require surgery after flaring up in France’s semi-final defeat.

Even the World Cup final would have had Arteta wincing, if he were not already hiding behind the sofa.

Merino caught a thunderous Lionel Messi shot straight to the face and uploaded a photo from the Spain dressing room afterwards to show off the damage.

The fact that the midfielder was icing his eye with a bottle of beer suggests he will be fine — and there will be a few sighs of relief among Arsenal’s medical staff.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It is their job now to manage the return of the club’s World Cup stars, who are due at least three weeks off.

Arsenal had 15 players at the tournament — including the now departed Leandro Trossard — with eight making it all the way to the final weekend.

In total, those from Arteta’s squad clocked up 4,224 pitch minutes during their time in North America.

Among Premier League clubs, only Manchester City players (5,925 minutes) had a higher total.



The situation is a headache for Arteta as it comes off the back of a season where Arsenal played 63 games. That campaign did not finish until May 30 and two days later Gunners players were jetting off to the World Cup.

They now finish the tournament with the sobering thought that the Premier League restarts in 30 days.

Arsenal go into the new season as the reigning champions but also sweating on the fitness of key trio Rice, Saka and Saliba.

The club expected many of their players would go deep at the World Cup, which is why pre-season has been tweaked.

There was a mini training camp in Marbella last week but the official start was Monday to reflect how late Arsenal finished last season.



A far-flung tour across the globe was also turned down and instead things will be more low-key.

They are having a training camp in Spain and will play their first friendly of pre-season in Girona on August 1. Four days later, they will face Real Betis in Dublin before heading back home to London.

A pair of friendlies at the Emirates complete the prep ahead of the Community Shield on August 16 against Manchester City in Cardiff.



Arsenal will hope this is a campaign where their injury record improves after making changes to the medical department.

Club doctor Zafar Iqbal and head of sports science and performance Tom Allen have both left.

Sam Wilson, lead physical performance coach, has also departed after being poached by Italian side Parma.

Three new hires have replaced them. Arnaldo Abrantes has joined from Aston Villa as club doctor.

Eneko Angulo arrives from Real Betis as a rehabilitation specialist.



And Bayer Leverkusen fitness coach Jose Jimenez has been added to the ranks with Wilson gone.

The trio will hope to resolve Arsenal’s injury issues, starting with getting Ben White and Jurrien Timber up to speed.

That would ease concerns over players returning late, but the situation presents an opportunity for youngsters.



The door is open for Max Dowman, 16, on the right flank, given Noni Madueke and Saka were away with England.

In midfield, Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly can both hope for minutes as Martin Zubimendi, Merino and Rice were at the World Cup until the final weekend.

Nwaneri faces an uncertain future right now, yet MLS showed towards the back end of last season how quickly things can change.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The 19-year-old looked set for the exit door — but ended up starting the Champions League final.

Him carrying on where he left off would ease Arteta’s headache at a time when the problems feel like they are already piling up.

Sports.title: Sturm Graz 4 Hearts 0: Champions League dream becomes a nightmare as awful defending costs Vrancken’s Jambos
Sports.content:
HAPHAZARD HEARTS couldn’t weather the Sturm as their Champions League hopes were blown away in Graz.

New boss Wouter Vrancken set up the Jambos to have a go at the Austrians in his first game in charge.



But a combination of poor defending and terrible finishing saw them on the end of a Euro hiding in a calamitous start to the Belgian’s Tynecastle reign.

Jon Gorenc Stankovic’s fourth minute header put Sturm ahead from a simple long throw into the Jambos box.



The Tynecastle side could still have gone in ahead at the break had Landry Kabore and Alexandros Kyziridis not missed sitters in front of goal.

And they paid the price when Graz hit them with a triple blow after the restart with Jeyland Mitchell, Luca Weinhandl and Jurgen Heil all taking advantage of more shambolic defending before the hour mark.

It means Tuesday’s return is now a dead rubber with the Gorgie outfit on their way into the Europa League.

With Benfica or St Gallen awaiting there, Vrancken will need to sort his side out quickly if they are to avoid a similar fate.

But time is not on his side as he tries to get his ideas across with games about to start coming thick and fast both at home and in Europe.

Many of the 1,300 Jambos fans who had travelled had spent the day hurtling down the tallest indoor slide in the world in Graz.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

The 170-metre Schlossbergrutsche twists all the way down from the clock tower overlooking the city.

Those brave enough can reach a top speed of 19 miles per hour on the 30-second journey to the bottom.

Little did they know their side’s hopes of taking anything from this tie would disappear even more quickly.

66 days had passed since that gut-wrenching final day loss to Celtic at Parkhead.

And so much had changed since with Derek McInnes, Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin all quitting for Rangers.



New boss Vrancken had only had limited time to work with the group of players he inherited from McInnes.

So it was perhaps no surprise he leaned on the majority of last season’s squad in his first game.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott and Calvin Miller were the only new boys to be given starts with Harry Milne chosen as captain.

German keeper Alexander Schwolow continued ahead of his move to Mainz at the end of the month.

Jamie McCart, Blair Spittal and Oisin McEntee were all included in a physical line-up.



And Landry Kabore was chosen up front with Miller, Claudio Braga and Alex Kyziridis in support.

Sturm faced Celtic and Rangers in the Europa League last season, losing to the Hoops but beating Gers.

And they got off to a flyer as they went ahead with less than four minutes gone.

The Jambos, in their new light grey away kit, had created the first two chances of the game through Kabore and Borchgrevink.

But when Mitchell’s long throw came into the box Kabroe lost skipper Stankovic who rose highest to head past Schwolow from six yards out.



It was a shocker of a goal to lose and the Tynecastle side rode their luck from another set piece soon after.

This time Jatta popped up at the back post to nod a corner onto the post as Schwolow scrambled to get across.

Schwolow stuck a leg out to keep out Jacob Hodl’s shot in the 17th minute after it took a deflection on its way through to goal.

But Hearts should have been back on terms in the 25th minute after Miller played in McEntee on the edge of the area.

He made his way past two challenges and pulled the ball back for Kabore just eight yards out but the striker’s low shot was straight at Khudiakov.



Kabore then set up Kyziridis only for the Greek winger to misfire in front of goal with Khudiakov making another straightforward stop.

And then Kyziridis missed an even better chance when Braga robbed Stankovic straight after, this time prodding the ball past the post.

The worry was all these missed chances would come back to haunt them.

It looked like that would happen when ref Bogar pointed to the spot when Milne slid in to deny Jatta in the 38th minute, the ball hitting his arm on the way.

Having been sent to the monitor to review the decision the whistler overturned the call.



It was the right decision and the Jambos went in at the break frustrated that they weren’t at least on level terms given the chances they had created.

But any hopes Hearts had of a comeback were snuffed out inside a crazy 10-minute spell at the start of the second half.

Mitchell all too easily headed home the second from sub Otar Kiteishvili’s corner at the back post in the 49th minute.

Weinhandl made it three four minutes later when his shot took a huge deflection off Milne and spun over Schwolow.

And Emran Soglo hit the post before Heil thumped Graz further ahead in the 59th minute from Weinhandl’s pass.



Vrancken threw on new signings Amadou Ba-Sy, Sabri Guendouz and Tom Renaud as he looked for a reaction from his shell-shocked side.

Renaud blazed wide after Ba-Sy had muscled his way into the home box.

But by that stage Sturm were in complete control as they cruised to a crushing win.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers completes record-breaking £117m Chelsea transfer from Aston Villa and becomes most expensive Brit ever
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS has become the most expensive British player ever after completing a transfer to Chelsea.

The England international has signed for the Blues from Aston Villa for £117million.



Rogers, 23, has signed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge with the option of a further year.

He said: “I’m so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I’ve always admired since I was a kid.



“I’m really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we’ve got and where the club is heading. That’s why I’m here and I can’t wait to get started.”

The deal eclipses the £116m paid by Manchester City to land fellow England World Cup star Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest earlier in the window.



Sandro Tonali‘s transfer to Tottenham from Newcastle also means it is the third deal of the summer to reach nine figures, while the window has only just hit the halfway mark.

Likewise, it breaks the £115m Chelsea paid for Moises Caicedo from Brighton in 2023.

Rogers is also now the second most expensive Premier League deal of all time, with only Alexander Isak‘s £130m move to Liverpool from Newcastle last summer trumping it.

He had his medical on Monday following the Three Lions’ third-place play-off against France.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rogers played the full 90 minutes of that clash as Thomas Tuchel‘s side won 6-4, making it his seventh appearance at the World Cup while registering two assists.

The attacking midfielder scored 14 goals and added 12 assists in all competitions last season under Unai Emery.

No Chelsea player registered more assists last season, while only Joao Pedro and Enzo Fernandez scored more than Rogers.

Rogers’ former club, Middlesbrough, will earn approximately £20m from the deal due to a clause meaning they will get 20 per cent of any profit Villa get from a sale.



Villa, who also sold Youri Tielemans to Manchester United earlier this month, signed Rogers from Boro for £15m.

The club released a statement to thank Rogers following his departure.

It read: “Aston Villa can confirm that Morgan Rogers has completed a permanent transfer to Chelsea.



“Since joining from Middlesbrough in 2024, the midfielder has enjoyed a rapid rise to prominence, helping Villa to lift the UEFA Europa League last term, scoring the third goal in the final in Istanbul.

“During his time at the club, he also earned his first senior England caps, representing his country at the FIFA World Cup 2026, where the Three Lions finished third.

“A player with impeccable behaviour and commitment, Morgan leaves Aston Villa with the best wishes of everyone at the football club for both his service to the club and for his future career.

“He will always remain a core part of our recent great moments and memories.”

Chelsea have shifted their transfer approach following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as manager.



The club finished 10th in the league last season, and are now taking drastic action to improve their squad with proven talent.

With Rogers having joined Chelsea from Villa, Alejandro Garnacho could be heading the other way.

Villa officials are hoping to sign the out-of-favour winger on loan with a buy clause included.

Sports.title: Tearful ex-Newcastle star Shola Ameobi pays emotional tribute to Kevin Keegan as he views tributes at St James’ Park
Sports.content:
EX-NEWCASTLE star Shola Ameobi paid an emotional tribute to former boss Kevin Keegan yesterday after his tragic death.

The ex-striker rubbed his eyes as he viewed a sea of flowers, scarves and footie tops left by fans at St James’ Park.



Nigeria ace Shola, 44, spent 14 years at Newcastle, scoring 53 goals, and is now a club ambassador.

King Kev, who died aged 75 after being diagnosed with stomach cancer, was his boss during his second spell as manager in 2008.



Hartlepool boss Lee Clark, who played under Keegan in the 1990s, also visited the makeshift shrine.

He said: “He was a hero at first, then my boss and friend.



“He was like the Pied Piper to the Geordie public. They adore him.”

Sir Alex Ferguson praised Keegan for building Newcastle’s “greatest team” in the 1990s when vying with Man United for the title.



Current Toon boss Eddie Howe said Keegan, who also played for Liverpool, Southampton and England, was an “inspiration”.

Morgan Rogers has hailed Chelsea as ‘the biggest club in London’ after Arsenal missed out on the England star. The Aston Villa midfielder was initially linked with a switch to the Emirates after his fine form in the Midlands.

‌



But Chelsea managed to hijack the move, sealing his services for £117m. Rogers was officially unveiled on Tuesday evening after undergoing a medical with his new employers.

‌



Speaking after his move was confirmed, he hailed Chelsea as the biggest club in the capital. The England star said: "I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho set to swap places with Morgan Rogers as Aston Villa eye swoop
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho set to swap places with Morgan Rogers as Aston Villa eye swoop

Chelsea have completed a £117m deal for Aston Villa and England star Morgan Rogers with former Manchester United man Alejandro Garnacho expected to go the other way to the Midlands

View 2 Images Chelsea are happy to let Garnacho leave (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea are set to get their wish for Alejandro Garnacho, with Aston Villa interested in signing the forward. The Blues only signed the Argentine frontman from Manchester United last summer in a £40m deal.

‌



But with Chelsea completing a £117m move for Villa and England star Morgan Rogers, the Blues are now happy to cut Garnacho adrift.

‌



Villa have already submitted a loan offer for him, with a conditional buy obligation attached and are close to finding an agreement. Chelsea initially wanted a permanent deal for the Argentine.

‌



Unai Emery is thought to be a big fan of Garnacho and is hoping to play a role in a career revival. Villa’s interest comes just days after new boss Xabi Alonso admitted that he was happy to let the forward leave.

He said: "Well the situation is that we have spoken with the sporting directors. There is an interest for him [Garnacho] from other clubs. So let's see how this develops. But hopefully, it finishes in the best possible way for other clubs."

West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Garnacho, 22, signed a seven-year deal with Chelsea last summer following his arrival from Old Trafford. He made 43 appearances across his debut season, scoring just eight goals, only one of which came in the Premier League.

‌



Garnacho would arrive at Villa as Rogers’ replacement following his own move to Chelsea. The former Middlesbrough man scored 14 times last term but Paul Merson is not convinced his move to West London is the right one.

He said: “It's a lot of money. Crazy money. Bringing Morgan Rogers in for £117m isn't what Chelsea needed.

“They've got Cole Palmer! They play in the same position! Rogers went to the World Cup instead of Palmer, because they play in the same position.

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho only joined Chelsea last summer (Image: Getty Images)

“Unless Chelsea go for the almighty and sell Enzo Fernandez - and swallow the pill for him, because he's not worth £100m - and then play Moises Caicedo at the base, then Rogers and Palmer both ahead of him.”

He continued: “Rogers has got to carry that price tag around with him. He will sit there and say: 'there is no pressure on me, I didn't pay that fee'. But it's a load of rubbish. Everybody will look at that when you don't do well.

‌



“A lot of people were saying it was too much for Declan Rice and Moises Caicedo when they moved for £100m. But the biggest compliment I can give them is nobody ever mentions it. They were good signings. That's what Rogers has got to hope for.

“But he's got to make things happen, which is a harder position to be in than Rice and Caicedo were. In midfield, you can do this and that - but Rogers will be judged on scoring and creating goals. That's the hardest job in the world.

“I'm also sure that at the start of last season, he was atrocious for Aston Villa. I'm sure he was. Then he came good and then had a good second part of the season.

Article continues below

“He can't play like that at Chelsea. That is an absolute no-go, it's a different ball game when you go for that kind of money.”

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers completes record-breaking £117m transfer to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers completes record-breaking £117m transfer to Chelsea

Chelsea have completed the capture of Morgan Rogers after beating Arsenal to a whopping £117million deal for one of England's World Cup stars

View 2 Images Rogers has put pen to paper on a seven-year deal at Stamford Bridge (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Morgan Rogers is officially a Chelsea player after finalising a transfer from Aston Villa which makes him the most expensive British footballer in history.

‌



The England star, 23, has put pen to paper on a contract until 2033 which includes an option for a further year. He moves to Stamford Bridge for a seismic £117million transfer fee, a figure which eclipses the amount Manchester City agreed to part with in order to acquire his World Cup team-mate, Elliot Anderson.

‌



Rogers was pursued for over two years by Chelsea, who beat off competition from Arsenal to sign the versatile attacking midfielder.

‌



Chelsea stole a march on Arsenal when the Gunners were unwilling to move from their valuation of the player, Mirror Football understands.

According to sources, the Gunners valued the England international at £80m, and were willing to pay a slight premium - but were left stunned when Chelsea agreed to pay a fee that makes Rogers' move the most expensive transfer of an Englishman in history - beating Anderson's move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City by £1m.

West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest READ MORE :

His capture is a first major win for the Blues' new manager, Xabi Alonso, who held productive talks with Rogers to help entice the former Middlesbrough man to west London.

‌



Upon finalising his move, Rogers said: "I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started.

“I’ve had a few conversations with him [Alonso] and I think it’s important for me to be here that I need to understand what the manager’s like, how he is and how he wants to operate.

‌



“It very much fits with the way I see the game, the way I want to play, and the way I want to be me, and be free and express myself. Him being a part of that was a massive factor in me being here.”

View 2 Images Rogers with new boss Xabi Alonso (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Rogers came through the youth academy at West Brom before moving to Man City in 2019. He didn't make a first-team appearance for City and went out on loan to Lincoln, Bournemouth and Blackpool.

‌



He joined Middlesbrough for an undisclosed fee in 2023 scoring five times in their run to the League Cup semi-finals. He joined Villa in the following January for £8m, potentially rising to £15m.

In all, Rogers made 125 appearances for Villa scoring 31 goals and helping them to the Europa League title last term.

On the international stage, Rogers made his senior England debut in November 2004 in a 3-0 victory against Greece in Athens. He has played 22 times for England, including at the recent World Cup, scoring once.

Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi 'reaches transfer agreement' after Man City, Man Utd and Arsenal interest

The Lille and Morocco midfielder is one of the most sought-after talents in Europe, with several Premier League clubs having been keeping a close eye on his situation

View 2 Images There is Premier League interest in Lille and Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Manchester City have reportedly reached an initial agreement with Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi over personal terms as they work on the transfer. Manchester United and Arsenal have both also been linked with the Morocco international.

‌



The 18-year-old is one of the most highly-rated talents in Europe, with teams queuing up to try and sign him this summer. He also caught the eye while representing Morocco in the World Cup.

‌



Despite his young age, Bouaddi played 42 times in all competitions for Lille last season and has become a key player for the Ligue 1 side. It’s reported that they will demand around €100 million (£85m) to sell him.

‌



Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub' READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Speaking earlier this month, Lille chairman Oliver Letang hinted at the price he wants. “When I see [Elliot] Anderson move to Manchester City for £116 million and [Sandro] Tonali to Tottenham for £100 million, and they don’t have the potential for development that Ayyoub has because he possesses unique qualities.

“I have a price in mind, and we’ll see what happens."

According to journalist Nicolo Schira, City have agreed a contract with the teenager that runs until 2031. The club will now continue talks with Lille to try and reach a club-to-club agreement over the transfer fee.

‌



It’s added that City expect two other ‘top European clubs’ to make a move, although it’s not said who those clubs are. Arsenal and United are two other clubs who have been heavily linked with an interest.

Former France international Emmanuel Petit has been full of praise about Bouaddi. "He's been one of the strongest young players in France,” he told talkSPORT

Sports.title: West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest
Sports.content:
West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest

Manchester United were among the clubs linked with a move for West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville but it appears that the Dutchman is set to move elsewhere

View 2 Images Summerville is set to leave West Ham after two years (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to lose out on Crysencio Summerville, with the West Ham star on the verge of a move to Saudi Arabia. The Red Devils were linked with a swoop for the Dutchman this summer, following the Hammers’ relegation from the Premier League.

‌



They were interested in him alongside Mateus Fernandes, who eventually completed a big-money move to Tottenham Hotspur. But United are also set to be frustrated in their pursuit of the former Leeds man.

‌



The Londoners have agreed a £68m deal with Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. Italian giants Roma were also interested but were only willing to offer around £39m.

‌



Summerville, who scored five Premier League goals last term, is now expected to undergo a medical ahead of completing his switch to the Middle East. West Ham in the meantime will aim to re-invest the considerable fee as they attempt to earn promotion from the Championship at the first time of asking.

The only signing that the Hammers have made so far is a deal for Venezuelan international Keiber Lamadrid. But one considerable boost has been Jarrod Bowen’s decision to commit his future to the club.

FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Speaking at the time, he said: "My main motivation is staying and bringing this club back to the Premier League where we belong. It was only right for me to speak at the right time. Ultimately it [relegation] hurt everyone and it should hurt everyone.

‌



"I flew out to Prague to meet (club directors) Daniel [Kretinsky] and Jiri [Svarc] and the ambition that I got from them, certainly in terms of the direction the club wants to move in, it interests me a lot. It didn't take a lot, because this club means a lot to me.

"For me, when you're here for a longer amount of time, you gain more affection, you grow into the club more, you grow into your role more and more, and I think that's what I've done.

View 2 Images Crysencio Summerville is expected to move to Saudi Arabia (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I've been here six and a half years and transitioned from a boy to a man and I've never tried to hide away from anything.

"There are things you can do better, but certainly in my character on the pitch and off the pitch, I never try and hide away from anything and shift the blame.

"I always try and stand up for them and just kind of live my life as captain of West Ham and also as a fan as well.

Article continues below

"I see myself in years to come as a West Ham fan. So, I always think 'what would they want as a fan if they got the opportunity to play on the pitch?'. For me, I think I'm like that character as well, so I think that's the way."

Sports.title: Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'
Sports.content:
Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has faced severe criticism during the World Cup for his close relationship with US President Donald Trump with controversial former chief Sepp Blatter among those to speak out

View 2 Images Sepp Blatter has taken a fresh swipe at Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Sepp Blatter has once again called for ‘new leadership’ at FIFA in a brutal dig at Gianni Infantino. The current president has faced serious criticism for a number of decisions throughout this summer’s World Cup.

‌



Ticket prices, over-commercialisation, as well as his close relationship with US President Donald Trump have all been issues. Criticism then sharply increased after the decision to suspend Folarin Balogun’s red card following a phone call from Trump.

‌



Blatter tore into Infantino immediately after that decision. Taking to Twitter, he said: “Red cards are not overturned by political phone calls. They are overturned by rules, evidence and independent bodies.

‌



"If a U.S. President intervenes with the FIFA President — and a player is suddenly cleared before a World Cup knockout match — the question is unavoidable: Quo vadis, FIFA? Quo vadis means 'Where are you going?' in Latin. Football must never become a playground for political power.”

Blatter has now doubled down with a fresh post calling for change right at the top of the organisation just days after the World Cup final.

Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked READ MORE :

He said: “The longest World Cup has come to an end - with the right champions. But on the way to the final whistle, the tournament had lost its credibility. Politics must not be allowed to overshadow the game. Now it is up to the fans, players and national associations to reclaim football and bring it back to its roots under new leadership.”

‌



While Blatter has called for fresh leadership, it appears that is unlikely. La Liga president Javier Tebas has claimed that due to a lack of opposition, it appears that Infantino is set to stay in charge.

Asked if he should quit, Tebas replied: "In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up." He added: "There's no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. He shouldn't stay, but the current state of affairs means he won't leave.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has faced plenty of criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"These past few days here in America, I've heard many people who are against Infantino, who disagree with what he's doing,

"They say it, but then they do nothing. I don't know what's worse, the silence or the complicity, because those who stay silent are perfectly aware of the damage football is suffering.

"The suspension of the American player's ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky that Belgium eliminated the USA, because otherwise a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won, they managed to bury the matter. But these things are just the tip of the iceberg."
