Sports.title: FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation
Sports.content:
FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation

Fenway Sports Group have confirmed that a consortium of investors, led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, have approached them about a significant minority stake in Liverpool

View 2 Images FSG are in talks over selling a minority stake in Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's owners have confirmed that a consortium of investors, spearheaded by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, have made an approach regarding a stake in the club. It is understood the group has the backing of the Mittal family, whose fortune was most recently estimated at more than £26billion by Forbes.

‌



No deal is currently in place and discussions remain at a preliminary stage, according to sources with knowledge of the situation. Bhatia was confirmed on Tuesday to have stepped down from his role as co-owner of Queens Park Rangers, with the London outfit announcing his exit on its official website.

‌



Bhatia is the son-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal, who heads up ArcelorMittal, the globe's biggest steel and mining firm, and Fenway Sports Group confirmed that active talks are underway over what has been characterised as a "significant minority stake".

‌



Kevin Keegan's final picture and brave public appearance before sad death aged 75 READ MORE :

Our sister title the Liverpool ECHO understand the discussions are being treated as comparable to the deal struck with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which was valued at between £82m and £164m. An FSG statement provided to the ECHO said: "An investment consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mr Bhatia has thus far refused to comment on the developments but made public his decision to resign from QPR on Tuesday, having joined the club at Loftus Road almost two decades ago. Bhatia said: "Since joining the club in 2007, QPR has been a deeply important part of my life, and of my family's life. Over nearly two decades we have shared promotions, relegations, unforgettable highs and painful lows, and the memories we have made at Loftus Road alongside the supporters will stay with us forever.

‌



View 2 Images Amit Bhatia could soon have a stake in Liverpool (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

"Being part of QPR has shaped me in many ways. It has taught me about resilience, responsibility and the importance of stewardship. I am especially proud of the work of QPR in the Community Trust, which reflects the best of the club and the extraordinary role it plays in the local community.

"I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection. I want to thank the players, managers, staff, the Community Trust, my fellow board members and, above all, the fans, who have made me and my family feel part of the QPR family for so many years.

‌



"I am grateful to my dear friend Ruben and his family for their friendship and partnership, as I am to Richard, Lee, Christian and everyone continuing to work on behalf of the club. QPR will always have a very special place in my heart."

FSG snapped up Liverpool for £300m back in October 2010. More than 15 years on, the 20-time Premier League champions have been valued at £5.2 billion by the prestigious American financial publication Forbes.

Earlier this year, the club recorded revenues exceeding £700m for the first time in their history.

Article continues below

In 2024, Fenway began exploring the possibility of establishing a multi-club ownership model, but have since put those plans on ice — a move that ultimately contributed to the departure of Michael Edwards, Liverpool's former sporting director, who had been appointed as FSG's CEO of football two years ago.

Sports.title: Hearts suffer chastening CL defeat in nightmare first game for Vrancken
Sports.content:
New Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken endured a nightmare debut as his side's Champions League hopes all but vanished with a 4-0 defeat against Sturm Graz.

Hearts lost set-piece goals in the early stages of each half and conceded twice more during a torrid spell before the hour mark.

The visitors missed two excellent chances and played some good football in the first half but they are left with a mountain to climb ahead of next Tuesday's second qualifying round second leg at Tynecastle.

Hearts look almost certain to drop into the Europa League, where they would face Benfica or Swiss side St Gallen, with the winners of this tie facing Fenerbahce or Gornik Zabrze.

Vrancken passed up the chance of guaranteed Europa League football with Sint-Truiden to replace Derek McInnes at Tynecastle with key players Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin following the manager to Rangers.

The Belgian named two debutants in his starting line-up, wide player Calvin Miller and centre-back Malachi Fagan-Walcott, while Jamie McCart was preferred to Stuart Findlay, one of Hearts' key players last season, in central defence.

Hearts also changed set-piece coaches in the summer with Liam Ross coming in for Ross Grant following his move to Celtic.

Set-plays were one of the team's strengths in their unlikely title challenge but they looked vulnerable from dead balls throughout.

Despite a promising start which saw Harry Milne force a save, Hearts conceded inside four minutes from a long throw. Jon Gorenc Stankovic ran away from his marker and outjumped McCart to head home.

Graz attacker Seedy Jatta headed off the post following a corner and Alexander Schwolow, who was selected despite sealing an imminent move to Mainz, saved an effort with his feet.

Hearts improved. Claudio Braga forced a save with a decent effort before Landry Kabore shot straight at the goalkeeper from 10 yards after a good run from Oisin McEntee. Alexandros Kyziridis soon missed an even better chance when he flicked the ball wide after good work from Braga.

The referee handed the Austrians a penalty for an extremely harsh handball decision against Milne before reversing the award following a look at his VAR monitor.

Graz dominated the opening stages of the second half and Jeyland Mitchell nodded home from close range after a 50th-minute corner. Schwolow seemed more concerned with pushing away an attacker than dealing with the inswinger, Kabore misjudged the flight and Mitchell shook off the attention of Braga.

Luca Weinhandl fired the third in off Milne three minutes later after the Hearts defence missed several chances to make a decisive challenge.

Schwolow stood motionless as Emran Soglo curled the ball off the inside of the far post and Jurgen Heil fired a shot through the goalkeeper at his near post after getting ample time and space to convert a return pass in the 59th minute.

Graz seemed to settle for four and Hearts could not get a lifeline.

McEntee made a mess of a free header, McCart failed to trouble the goalkeeper from a string of headed chances and Tom Renaud twice fired over from 22 yards.

Sports.title: Draper misses out on US Open main draw - will have to qualify
Sports.content:
Former British No 1 Jack Draper is set to have to qualify for the US Open this year as the 2024 semi-finalist missed out on a spot in the main draw.

Draper is poised to return to action at the DC Open in Washington from July 27 after missing Wimbledon due to a recurrence of bone bruising in his left arm.

The injury was the latest blow for the 24-year-old, who has managed only a handful of tournaments since first stepping away from the tour a year ago with the same issue.

Draper's ranking has taken a hit as a result, dropping down to 147th in the world, resulting in him having to likely qualify in order to play the fourth and final Grand Slam of the season.

Arthur Fery, the new British men's No 1, will feature at Flushing Meadows for the first time in his career after his remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wild card has seen his ranking soar to 36th in the world.

Both he and Emma Raducanu, the 2021 US Open champion, are just outside of the top 32 seeds, however, with Raducanu ranked 37th.

Image: Emma Raducanu is ranked 37th in the world, just outside of one of the top 32 seeds

They're joined by fellow British hopefuls Cam Norrie, Jan Choinski and Katie Boulter in the main draw for when the tournament gets under way on August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and Wimbledon winner Jannik Sinner will lead the fields for the respective women's and men's singles in New York.

Sabalenka will look to become the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, while Sinner will be trying to regain the title that Carlos Alcaraz took from the 2024 champion when they met in last year's final.

Image: Jannik Sinner retained his Wimbledon men's singles title earlier this month

The top-ranked Italian is coming off his fifth major championship, after beating French Open winner Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final.

Alcaraz, who has missed the last two majors because of a wrist injury but hopes to return during the North American hard-court swing, is ranked as the third seed and entered in the field.

Sports.title: 'Rock star' Woad excited to return to scene of stunning pro debut win
Sports.content:
Lottie Woad returns to the scene of her stunning debut win as a professional this week when looking to defend the ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open.

Last year, the then 21-year-old took a two-shot lead into the final day at Dundonald Links, managing to hold off Hyo Joo Kim and the chasing pack to take the title.

In doing so, Woad became just the third player in LPGA Tour history to win on her first professional start, following on from Rose Zhang in 2023 and Beverly Hanson in 1951.

"I didn't appreciate at the time, obviously being my first event," Woad said ahead of her return this week - the Scottish Open, live on Sky Sports Golf from 9.30am on Thursday.

"I didn't know what to expect. But now I've been playing every week and playing with the same people and obviously seeing how good everyone is, it definitely feels more special now.

"Very excited to be back. It's a little different to last year, I've got the family here as well. It will be a fun week."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lottie Woad reflected on her first LPGA Tour victory on her professional debut at the Scottish Open.

Woad's triumph in 2025 was exactly as she describes it, special, seeing her deliver immediately in the pro ranks on her long-touted talent that shone as an amateur.

Her name first floated onto the radar in May 2022 when making her debut on the Ladies European Tour in a 10th-placed finish at the Madrid Open, before she enrolled at Florida State where she would become WGCA Freshman of the Year, a junior FSU Female Athlete of the Year and ACC Golfer of the Year.

She continued her rise in April 2024 by winning the Augusta National Women's Amateur, while she'd later claim the No 1 spot in the World Amateur Golf Rankings and became the first English woman to win the Mark H. McCormack Medal as the leading amateur in the world.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Amundi Evian Championship as Lottie Woad topped the leaderboard.

She was the leading amateur when she finished tied-10th at the 2024 AIG Women's Open, while her Scottish Open triumph last year followed a maiden LET victory at the KPMG Women's Irish Open and a narrow miss at making history as an amateur at the Amundi Evian Championship.

That tied-third finish has since been followed by further major top-10s at the 2025 Women's Open (eighth) and 2026 Chevron Championship (seventh), while she held the halfway lead at the 2026 Evian Championship two weeks ago before fading to a tied-16th finish.

The 22-year-old already sits a remarkable fifth in the Rolex Women's World Rankings, registering a second LPGA Tour win at the Kroger Queen City Championship in May.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the Queen City Championship, where Lottie Woad won her second LPGA Tour title.

"It's definitely been a long year," Woad reflected. "I've played a lot of golf, had a lot of new experiences.

"I've definitely learned some things as well in the year.

"It's nice to come back to where I guess it all started, my pro debut here. I've been happy with how I've been playing.

"At Evian, it wasn't the weekend I wanted there. But I'm trying to take what I can from that, still playing good golf but also learning too."

During Woad's Scottish Open victory last year that kick-started her pro career, she was grouped with world No 1 Nelly Korda.

"She's not afraid to compete against the biggest names in the game," Sky Sports Golf's Dame Laura Davies said at the time. "She has every part of her game, and her results already suggest she has all the qualities to become a rockstar of the future."

And 'rock star' Woad could well be the headline act this time round as she's again grouped with Korda and Hull for the opening two rounds of her title defence at Dundonald Links.

Not that the modest Woad sees it that way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Nelly Korda's US Women's Open win after a thrilling final round.

Speaking on Korda, who has doubled her career major tally to four with wins at the Chevron and US Women's Open this year, Woad said: "I think every event she's at, she's the person everybody is coming to see. She's No 1 in the world.

"Last year I was playing with her and we got a really big crowd. Playing with her again this year so I expect it to be the same.

"I hope it goes same as last year."

Who will win the ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open? Watch exclusively live from July 23-26 on Sky Sports Golf. Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Curran, Pooran blast defending champs MI London past SunRisers in Hundred opener
Sports.content:
MI London began their pursuit of a fourth successive Hundred title with a commanding seven-wicket victory over SunRisers Leeds at The Kia Oval, as the new-look competition got under way.

The 2026 edition of The Hundred had a different feel to it with name and kit changes following heavy overseas investment but MI London, formerly known as Oval Invincibles, ensured some things remained constant.

Chasing 144 for an opening-night victory, Sam Curran (60no off 39) and Nicholas Pooran (58no off 22) produced a blistering 93-run fourth-wicket partnership as the defending champions weathered the early loss of Will Jacks and Jason Roy to cruise to victory with 16 balls to spare.

Score summary – MI London Women vs SunRisers Leeds Men Sunrisers Leeds 143 from 99 balls: Mitchell Marsh (41 off 27), Ryan Rickelton (25 off 16), Tom Alsop (31 off 18); Richard Gleeson (4-25), Sam Curran (2-27) MI London 144-3 from 84 balls: Sam Curran (60no off 39), Nicholas Pooran (58no off 22); Brydon Carse (2-18); Nathan Ellis (1-22)

SunRisers, who appeared in last year's competition under the Northern Superchargers name, had earlier been bowled out for 143 runs in 99 balls, with the big-hitting Mitchell Marsh (41 off 27) and Ryan Rickleton (25 off 16) top scoring before Richard Gleeson (4-25) ripped through the order.

Rickelton blasted three sixes as he put on 40 for the first wicket alongside Marsh before he was brilliantly trapped lbw by a trademark Sam Curran slower ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Six and out for Harry Brook! The England captain falls after scoring just eight runs for the SunRisers against MI London in The Hundred.

His replacement, England white-ball captain Harry Brook, lasted just seven balls, holing out to Rashid Khan on eight the ball after smashing Nathan Sowter for six.

Marsh steadied, striking three fours and three sixes before being undone by the Curran brothers, chipping a slower ball from Tom into the hands of Sam at cover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Curran combo! Tom's 'beauty' of a delivery is rewarded with catch by his brother Sam.

With captain Zak Crawley (13 off 11) unable to kick the SunRisers into gear, it was left to Tom Alsop's 31 off 18 balls to help post a respectable total before Gleeson removed Nathan Ellis to wrap up their innings with a ball to spare.

Carse removed Jacks and Roy with the sixth and eighth balls of his opening spell as MI London suffered an early wobble in their run chase.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Outrageous! Abrar Ahmed hits Richard Gleeson's hat-trick ball for a massive six!

But after James Vince was bowled by Ellis, Pooran and Curran steadied the ship with a rapid-fire 50-run stand from 23 balls.

Curran brought up his fifty in 34 balls before Pooran reached his in 19, as the pair shared 10 fours and eight sixes to propel MI London to victory with plenty in reserve.

Captain Curran: I can read the game well

MI London captain Sam Curran:

"I did a little bit last year trying to work on things and it helps that I have captained for Surrey in the Blast and in the ILT20.

"I feel I can read the game quite well and that I can anchor run chases. I think I read the game well as I bowl.

"But I don't feel like a captain as there are so many good voices. I have so many great brains around and it is nice to start a tournament well."

Pooran: We just tried to stay positive

Meerkat Match Hero, Nicholas Pooran:

"I came in and did exactly what I needed to do.

"We just tried to stay as positive as we could. It was all about hitting a few boundaries and trying to take the partnership all the way to the end.

"Scoring runs gives you confidence but winning games is more important to me and I am happy we got off to the right start at home."

What's next?

Wednesday's Hundred double-header comes from the Utilita Bowl in Southampton as Southern Brave take on Welsh Fire. The women's game starts at 2.45pm, with the men's match under way from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Broad: England Test job less attractive than it was
Sports.content:
Former England bowler Stuart Broad says he understands Andy Flower's decision to turn down the England Test job, and is unsure over who the ECB turn to next, pondering whether the role has become "less attractive".

Brendon McCullum was removed as England's Test head coach after a run of seven defeats in nine and Flower, who led the team to victory in the three Ashes series during his previous spell in charge between 2009 and 2014, quickly emerged as the favourite to replace him.

But Flower cited his current coaching commitments with Indian Premier League franchise Royal Challengers Bengaluru, as well as The Hundred's London Spirit - which would overlap with the English cricket season - as a reason to rule himself out of contention.

Image: Andy Flower was previously coach of Trent Rockets in The Hundred but will be in charge of London Sprit for the 2026 tournament

"Andy Flower is one of the best coaches in the world," Broad told Sky Sports News. "He's done brilliantly with RCB to win back-to-back IPL titles. And he's now gone to the London Spirit from the Trent Rockets.

"I support his decision, really. He's got a very comfortable, steady job at the moment. He's got two brilliant franchises that he works with consistently and he's growing something very special.

"Would he want to leave that for the pressures of and the unknown of the ECB and the Test match job at the moment? Probably not."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton discuss who they think should replace Brendon McCullum as the England Test head coach.

Broad added: "Five, 10 years ago, this was a very sought-after job. I think with the franchise world that surrounds cricket at the moment, it's less attractive.

"But it's still attractive to the right person, and there will be people keen to do that job."

Justin Langer, Darren Lehmann and Jonathan Trott are some of the other names to have been linked with the England Test job.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southern Brave and Australia all-rounder Marcus Stoinis says Justin Langer's work ethic would make him a good choice if selected to be England's next men's Test head coach.

Broad has "absolutely no idea" who the ECB turn to next, but warned that the "grass isn't always greener" as they look to replace McCullum.

"I saw a very positive side to Brendon McCullum," Broad said. "I'm not saying that results were acceptable at all, in the last year really.

"But unless you get someone better than McCullum, then it's a poor decision. So I'm very interested to see what's coming.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Cole breaks down Brendon McCullum's departure from his role as England Test coach and looks into why 'something had to give' for the ECB.

"I don't know who's on their shortlist. I heard [ECB chief executive] Richard Gould talk about succession planning, that they have six to 10 names for every role.

"I don't know how true that can be if the first guy you go to says 'no, I'm not interested.'"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stuart Broad's reaction to news that Jacob Bethell will miss The Hundred due to a knee injury he picked up on England duty in the ODI series with India.

'Difficult for Brook to captain in all three formats'

England also have to name a replacement Test captain following Ben Stokes' retirement during the series-ending Test defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June.

Harry Brook was Stokes' vice-captain and is currently in charge of the white-ball sides, leading to workload concerns if he were to also take the Test job - along with how the move would look after Brook was disciplined during the winter following an altercation with a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand the day before captaining an ODI.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook pays tribute to Ben Stokes following his retirement from international cricket and insists that he is up to the challenge of becoming the next England Test captain.

"I think [captaining] three formats is difficult depending on how long you do it," Broad said. "Ultimately, he's one of our best players, so you want him fulfilling his potential with the bat.

"He's done a brilliant job with the T20 side, particularly, and the question will be whether he wants to give that away with T20 World Cups that come around every couple of years?

"He's also got a 50-over World Cup next October in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, in what will feel like English conditions and will suit them.

"Does he want to give that away to then focus on the Test match job, which brings its own challenges and pressures? There's definitely more pressure in the Test match job than there is in white ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eoin Morgan and Michael Atherton debate what the next steps are for England cricket after Ben Stokes' retirement.

"It's a really interesting call for [director of men's cricket] Rob Key. There's a lot on his shoulders at the minute.

"It's been a disastrous start to the summer from his and England's point of view after the so-called reset [following the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter].

"Really big decisions coming their way, and Harry Brook will probably have a decision to make at some stage."

Sports.title: Could the World Cup be back in the US as soon as 2038? Absolutely
Sports.content:
As is often the case, it has been left to Donald Trump to say the quiet bit out loud. “We have to do this again and we have to do it while I’m around, you hear that Gianni?” the US president told Fox News in an interview broadcast in the buildup to the World Cup final.

An American bid for the 2038 World Cup has been the talk of the hotel lobbies populated by administrators from around the world over the past month, who have watched this country’s seemingly limitless appetite for major events and willingness to pay whatever it takes to attend them.

Fifa has been quietly, but actively encouraging a US bid for some time and in a meeting at the Waldorf Astoria on Park Avenue in New York on Saturday it became clearer why.

The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, told representatives of the governing body’s 211 member associations that its revenue projections for the current four-year cycle has increased from $11bn (£8.2bn) to $15bn, with the vast majority of the growth coming from an explosion in ticketing and hospitality revenue.

A Fifa source disclosed that such has been the demand in the US in particular that ticketing and hospitality sales have gone past $5bn, with that part of the market now worth more than the World Cup’s TV rights for the first time.

“Fifa will want to get back here as quickly as possible,” said a senior figure at one of its hospitality partners.

While ticket sales have exceeded expectations, helped by the dynamic pricing and secondary market resale models that are embedded in US culture, in one crucial respect Fifa left a huge amount of money on the table, another reason it is desperate to return.

In an extraordinary deal, Fox Sports was awarded English-language TV rights in the US by Fifa without a bidding process, a precautionary move by the world governing body to prevent a lawsuit when Qatar 2022 was moved to the winter after the TV contracts had already been signed, creating a direct clash with the US domestic sports season, particularly the NFL and NBA.

With no competitive tension, Fox was given a relative bargain, paying $485m for the 2026 rights, the same as in Qatar, despite the World Cup having an extra 40 matches and taking place on home soil. For context, the NFL’s domestic TV deal is worth $11bn a year, with the NBA bringing in around $7bn.

Fox has capitalised this summer as a result, on the back of bumper viewing, with industry experts predicting it will make more than $1bn from TV adverts, whose volume and value has increased due to the addition of hydration breaks.

Fifa is determined to recoup what many regard as lost income from the US market in future TV rights cycles.

Having watched with frustration as Fox has cashed in, ESPN and NBC are expected to bid for the 2030 tournament, while initial conversations have also taken place with Netflix about them joining in the auction.

View image in fullscreen High prices did not deter fans from packing out stadiums at the World Cup in the US. Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP

Netflix has already signalled its growing interest in football by buying American rights for the Women’s World Cup in 2027 and 2031, the latter being held in the US, and another men’s tournament seven years later would spark another boom.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No country has hosted the World Cup twice in 12 years, but Fifa’s statutes and recent staging decisions give it the flexibility for this to happen.

By taking the 2030 World Cup to three continents and six countries – Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay – before Saudi Arabia hosts in 2034, a North American bid for 2038 is permitted under Fifa’s confederation rotation policy, along with one from Oceania.

Soccer Australia had wanted to bid for 2034, but after being given less than a month to formally register its interest by Fifa, withdrew its candidacy leaving Saudi Arabia to be selected unopposed, Infantino’s preferred method.

To complicate matters slightly, the North American confederation, Concacaf, is understood to have reservations about another US bid as it wants to give opportunities to other members.

Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico have been added to the 2031 Women’s World Cup bid and another joint endeavour could emerge, although unsurprisingly Trump would prefer the US to be sole hosts. “Based on the numbers we will be requesting it again immediately,” he told Fox.

Fifa’s timeline for opening the 2038 process is not yet known, but history suggests it could move quickly to secure the outcome it wants. The sudden opening of the 2034 bidding process in October 2024 took most confederations by surprise with Infantino announcing that Saudi Arabia would be the hosts just 25 days later, a decision ratified by all Fifa members at a bizarre virtual extraordinary general meeting two months later.

Infantino will be re-elected for a fourth full term at next year’s Fifa Congress in Morocco, almost certainly unopposed, and then all eyes will turn to the 2038 contest.

Barring what would be an unprecedented change to the US constitution to permit an additional term, Trump is due to leave office in January 2029, which may quickly become the deadline for Fifa.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers ‘excited to join biggest club in London’ after making £117m Chelsea move
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers has joined Chelsea from Aston Villa for a fee of £117m, signing a seven-year deal to become the Blues’ record signing.

A deal was agreed on Saturday for the 23-year-old to move to Stamford Bridge as the club stole in ahead of Arsenal, who had been in talks to sign the England international and had appeared to be favourites to secure his signature.

It is understood that the chance to work with the new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso was a key factor in persuading Rogers, who has just returned from helping England to a third-place finish at the World Cup, to choose west London.

He started in the 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday as well as the 6-4 win over France on Saturday that earned the bronze medal. He told his new club’s website: “I’m so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I’ve always admired since I was a kid. I’m really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we’ve got and where the club is heading. That’s why I’m here and I can’t wait to get started.”

A versatile forward who satisfies Chelsea’s need for a player that can play multiple attacking roles, he has enjoyed a rapid rise at Villa Park following his move from Middlesbrough in January 2024 and helped fire Villa to a top-four finish and the Europa League last season.

He leaves Villa having scored 31 times in 125 appearances under Unai Emery.

The deal represents one of the most significant buys of Chelsea owners BlueCo’s four-year reign. Co-owner Behdad Eghbali indicated towards the end of last season that the club had learned the lessons of an underwhelming campaign in which the team finished 10th and were thrashed in the Champions League last 16 by Paris Saint-Germain, and that they would be targeting players in the market that would be in a position to help them challenge for the title.

View image in fullscreen Rogers walks on the pitch at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

The former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich midfielder Alonso, a two-time Champions League winner as a player, was hired partly in order to convince the right calibre of player to move to Chelsea.

The deal for Rogers is arguably the biggest the club have pulled off since Cole Palmer moved from Manchester City in 2023. Rogers becomes the fourth signing of the summer as the Blues overhaul their squad, following the arrivals of defender Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha and winger Geovany Quenda.

In June, the club failed in an attempt to reunite Alonso with Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, with Chelsea unwilling to meet the Black Cats’ valuation of a player who will turn 34 in September.

Sports.title: Iraola determined to keep Mac Allister and Alisson at Liverpool this season
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has said he is determined to keep Alexis Mac Allister and Alisson for his first season as Liverpool head coach and must strengthen a squad that will be without Hugo Ekitiké and Conor Bradley for several more months.

The dust had barely settled on Argentina’s World Cup final defeat by Spain when Mac Allister was linked with a move to Real Madrid. Iraola, in Chicago for the start of Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US, accepted the midfielder is unlikely to be 100% ready for the Premier League opener at Newcastle due to a post-World Cup holiday. But he allayed doubts over Mac Allister’s long-term future at Liverpool, where he is under contract until 2028, by insisting the 27-year-old is part of next season’s plans.

Iraola said: “I think Alexis has been one of the best players at the club for the last few years, and he has had a very good World Cup, so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in other markets. But I want to keep my good players. I’m looking forward more to signing new players rather than losing the ones we have here.”

Alisson is another established figure whose Liverpool future has been questioned, with the Brazil international strongly linked with Juventus at the end of last season. Iraola has not met Alisson or Mac Allister in person due to their World Cup commitments but has spoken with both, and guaranteed the former will remain a Liverpool player next season.

“I am very happy with the situation we have right now in the goalkeeping area,” said Iraola. “We have Alisson, we have Giorgi [Mamardashvili]. Now we are going to send Armin [Pecsi] on loan but we have the guarantee of the three keepers here. Freddie [Woodman] played some games last season, I think it is a guarantee for us.

“Alisson is also someone in a changing room that has lots of references, in terms of experience. He is someone that definitely will help us in this process of adaptation of the new signings and the young players. We need the references like Virgil [van Dijk], Alisson, Joe Gomez; players that have been here for a long time, and I am sure we will have this help.”

Liverpool have brought a young squad on their US tour, which currently involves a training camp at Chicago Fire before the first game against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch will join the tour next week when Van Dijk, Cody Gakpo and Alisson will begin their pre-season training regimes back on Merseyside.

Iraola admitted Liverpool are “very thin” in terms of defensive numbers and while a fit Bradley would be considered first choice at right-back, his recovery from a serious knee injury sustained in January means the club could be forced into the market.

“Stefan [Bajcetic] and Wataru [Endo] are close to training with the group,” he said. “With the others [injured players], we’ll have to wait more. The closest one to returning after that is [Giovanni] Leoni. Conor and Hugo are way off. We are talking about months.”

Sports.title: Liverpool owner FSG in talks to sell 30% stake to Amit Bhatia consortium for £1.35bn
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s owner is in talks over ­selling a minority stake to a consortium led by the former Queens Park Rangers co‑owner Amit ­Bhatia and backed by his father-in-law ­Lakshmi Mittal, the billionaire Indian steel magnate. The Guardian understands a sale of 30% of the club is being discussed, with an offer of around £1.35bn on the table.

Fenway Sports Group confirmed in a statement to the Financial Times that it had begun negotiations with a group led by Bhatia over a ­potential minority share sale that would value ­Liverpool at about £4.5bn.

“An investment consortium led and ­managed by Amit Bhatia has expressed ­interest in ­making a strategic ­minority ­investment in Liverpool Football Club,” the statement said.

It is believed that talks over the deal have been going on for three months.

FSG paid £300m to take ­control of Liverpool in 2010 and is poised to secure a spectacular return on its investment. The ­Boston‑based group, led by John W Henry, which also owns the ­Boston Red Sox and Pittsburgh ­Penguins, has pre­viously held discussions over a minority sale without reaching agreement but, with the Mittal family ­possessing an estimated net worth of £23bn, there is no doubt the buyers have the resources to execute the transaction.

Industry sources expressed surprise at the purported £4.5bn valuation but it is in line with recent deals.

Chelsea were bought four years ago by the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital group for an overall £4.25bn, although £2.5bn was to purchase the shares from Roman Abramovich. These proceeds were deposited into a frozen UK bank account while £1.75bn was a legally binding commitment for future investment directly into the club. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s purchase of 25% of Manchester United in 2024 valued the club at £4.3bn.

In an indication of the ­seriousness of the consortium’s bid for ­Liverpool, Bhatia resigned as a director of QPR on Tuesday after 19 years. The ­London-born entrepreneur has held numerous leadership roles at QPR since investing in the club in 2007. He said: “QPR has been a deeply important part of my life, and of my family’s life … I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection.”

Liverpool are in the US under their new head coach, Andoni Iraola, for a pre-season tour which begins with a game against Sunderland in ­Nashville on Saturday.

Sports.title: Manchester United supporters groups in uproar over suspension of season tickets
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s official Fans’ Forum, Manchester United Suppor­ters Trust (Must), The 1958 and five other such groups have complained to the club over supporters being “treated as suspects” after some had season tickets suspended as part of a move to stop the illegal reselling of seats.

United last week contacted fans who used six or more devices to access accounts linked to the club or to forward tickets, as in their view this suggested the potential buying of seats to resell. Members are allowed only to forward tickets to other members, or sell them back to United.

Those contacted were asked why multiple accounts were accessed, to identify the differing devices they used, and for photo ID to prove their validity. “Following a detailed review of acti­vity across our ­ticketing and digital platforms, we have ­identified sustained activity associated with your account, or with accounts that appear to be connected to or ­controlled by you, which may indicate a breach of the club’s ticketing terms and conditions,” the email from United said.

In a joint ­statement, ­supporter groups said: “Professional touting, automated purchasing and those who exploit ­supporters for ­financial gain have no place at ­Manchester United and deserve robust action. However, that action must be fair, ­proportionate and ­transparent. Longstanding supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, should never feel they are being treated as suspects ­without clear evidence, due process or a meaningful opportunity to respond to the allegations made against them. The current approach has created a growing perception among supporters of ‘ban first and ask questions later’.

“The Fans’ Forum has rightly called on the club to pause the ­issuing of further suspensions and to halt any cancellation of season tickets while meaningful discussions take place. We support this.”

Reasons given by fans for the use of multiple devices to access club accounts includes being able to act for a group of friends or for elderly family members who struggle to use technology. United’s position is understood to be that no bans or formal sanctions have been applied and that any season tickets that have been revoked will be reissued before the team’s first home game of the season, which is against Ipswich Town on 30 August.

United have applied restrictions to accounts and offered only three days to appeal once a verdict is reached, as the club believe some of these are being used for illegal resale and the usual 14 days could be used to sell tickets on.

Sports.title: ‘The scrutiny is constant’: referee Anthony Taylor retires from football
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from elite refereeing after a distinguished career spanning more than two decades and 831 matches.

One of England’s most accomplished officials, the 47-year-old officiated 668 matches in the professional game in England. He brings the curtain down on his career following his final appointment – the World Cup last‑16 game between Portugal and Spain in the US.

Reflecting on his career, Taylor said: “Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.

“I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants, Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years. Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.”

Over 16 Premier League seasons, Taylor took charge of 432 top-flight matches and officiated every major domestic cup final. His honours include the FA Cup finals in 2017 and 2020, the 2015 League Cup final, the 2015 Community Shield and the 2018 Championship playoff final.

Taylor also enjoyed an outstanding international career, spending 14 years on the Fifa international list. During that time, he officiated at two World Cups (2022 and 2026), two European Championships (2020 and 2024) and two Club World Cups (2022 and 2025).

Quick Guide How do I 

Across the 163 international matches of which he took charge Taylor was entrusted with some of world football’s biggest fixtures, including the 2020 Uefa Super Cup, the 2021 Nations League final, the 2022 Club World Cup final, the 2023 Europa League final and the 2024 Champions League semi-final.

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, said: “Anthony has been a fantastic servant to the game over many years, both domestically and on the international stage. He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games including Portugal against Spain in this summer’s World Cup which ultimately capped off an outstanding career.

“He’s consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it’s not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many. The professionalism he’s shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.

“We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career.”

Sports.title: ‘The utmost respect for him’: Alex Ferguson pays tribute to Kevin Keegan
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson has saluted Kevin Keegan for building Newcastle’s “greatest team”. Keegan, who had cancer, died on Monday at the age of 75 and Ferguson has joined the tributes for one of football’s most endearing characters.

Ferguson and Keegan were involved a fierce battle for Premier League supremacy, with Ferguson’s Manchester United pipping Newcastle to the title in 1996. “I had the utmost respect for him,” Ferguson told Track Radio. “We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic. He re-energised that club and he brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism great supporters can give.

“And he also brought three great players to the club – [David] Ginola, [Faustino] Asprilla, Philippe Albert – and added a bit of class to the team. The challenges we had with Newcastle at that time were huge.”

Keegan, frustrated by Ferguson’s comments in the media towards the end of the tense title fight, memorably ranted at the Scot in a television interview. Despite that, Ferguson remained friendly with the former Liverpool and England striker and admired Keegan’s impressive rebuilding job at Newcastle.

The club were in danger of relegation to the third tier when Keegan took over, but he saved them from that fate and then won promotion to the Premier League in 1993. Keegan made Newcastle so dynamic they were referred to as “the entertainers”.

Ferguson believes the title runners-up were the best team in the club’s history. “Kevin carried the love of the game on his sleeve, there’s no question about that, and that carried right on to the fans, to the players,” he said. “That period at Newcastle was of emotion, it was excitement. They brought these great players to the club and they added to it, and it gave Newcastle – I think – their best ever team.”

View image in fullscreen Tributes at St James’ Park for Kevin Keegan, who died on Monday. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

Ferguson said he and Keegan had bumped into each other at a pub near Wentworth golf club a few weeks after that season. They spent the night around a piano with all thoughts of the rivalry forgotten. “The great thing about him, he held no grudges,” Ferguson said. “That was a fantastic quality he had and we had a great night.

Sports.title: ‘Reclaim football’: Sepp Blatter joins La Liga chief in call for Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has come in for heavy criticism from his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, and the La Liga president, Javier Tebas, with the pair united in the belief that he should stand down.

As Spain celebrated their World Cup win on Sunday, Tebas accused Infantino of “destroying the football industry” by prioritising the World Cup over national competitions. He claimed “his time is up”. Blatter has called for “fans, players and national associations to reclaim football and bring it back to its roots under new leadership”.

Tebas is particularly opposed to the Fifa president’s enthusiasm for expanding the 2030 tournament to 64 teams from 48. “Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas told Italy’s La Gazzetta dello Sport.

“The football industry is not just the World Cup. Not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They [Fifa] are destroying the football industry, which generates tens of thousands of jobs, for an event that lasts 40 days and involves a minority of players. We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise they are making irresponsible decisions.”

Tebas believes Infantino should resign, although he admits he finds it hard to envisage such a scenario. “He has the support of the system, of the federations. There is no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. It is a system rotten at its core.”

Scandal-proof: why Infantino’s Fifa power can’t be touched – video

After 10 years at Fifa’s helm, Infantino is poised to be re‑elected for a fourth term in March, potentially standing unopposed for the third time in a row, but Tebas believed the Swiss was a World Cup win away from being forced out. He argues that had the USA defeated Belgium in their last‑16 game Infantino might been mired in an unrecoverable scandal.

The USA striker Folarin Balogun had a one-match ban suspended by the Fifa disciplinary committee, facilitating his involvement against Belgium. The decision was taken after a phone call made to Infantino by Donald Trump. Infantino said the decision to overturn Balogun’s ban was made independently by its disciplinary committee “based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts”.

Tebas said: “The suspension of the American player’s ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky Belgium eliminated the USA because a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won they were able to bury the matter. But these things are just the tip of the iceberg.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Blatter, a controversial figure during his tenure as Fifa president, appears to regard the Balogun case as a tipping point. “The longest World Cup has come to an end with the right champions,” he wrote on X. “But on the way to the final whistle, the tournament lost its credibility. Politics must not be allowed to overshadow the game.”

Tebas feels much the same about hydration breaks and extended half‑time intervals. “Fifa arranges things as it wants, for what it wants, for its own interests, certainly not football,” he said. “So if they need a 27-minute half-time break, they’ll have it.

“Hydration breaks are a lie. We have them in La Liga, but when it’s genuinely hot. The pitches in Dallas, Los Angeles, Atlanta had air conditioning; I had to put a jumper on in the stands. It was a lie, a break for advertising.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: New boss Vrancken laments Hearts' failings after nightmare first match in charge
Sports.content:
New boss Vrancken laments Hearts' failings after nightmare first match in charge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wouter Vrancken bemoaned his players’ lack of efficiency in both boxes as Hearts slumped to a nightmare 4-0 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League second qualifying round tie in Austria.

It was a horrendous first match in charge for Belgian coach Vrancken who replaced Derek McInnes in the Hearts hot seat this summer.

Despite dominating possession and having more touches in the opposition box than Sturm Graz, Vrancken’s side suffered a crushing loss which effectively ends their hopes of further progress in Europe’s elite club competition.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken despairs as his new charges suffer in Austria

Hearts were guilty of shocking defending, especially at set pieces, as goals from Jon Stankovic, Jeyland Mitchell, Luca Weindhandl and Jurgen Heil put Graz in total control.

The visitors also missed several clear-cut chances of their own with Pierre Landry-Kabore and Alexander Kyziridis especially culpable when the score was still 1-0.

‘We didn’t start too badly but then conceded from a set piece,’ said Vrancken. ‘That was the summary of the game, we got killed by two set pieces at the start of the first half and second half.

‘After the first goal, we needed some minutes to come back into it and find our confidence again. We did pretty well and created a lot of chances which we needed to do much better with.

‘They were 100 per cent chances and at this level, you have to score them. I was pretty confident at half-time that we could still turn it around.

‘Then the second half started and after we missed the first good opportunity again, we conceded from another set piece.

Graz celebrate after Stankovic scores the early opening goal for Graz

‘Then it is difficult in their heads for the players. Sometimes you try to force it and make it more difficult for yourself. When you don’t kill (teams) yourself, you get killed. It’s a pity.

‘We had to be more efficient and Sturm Graz were more efficient than us tonight. It’s no excuse. We showed in the game that we had a lot of possession and created a lot of chances from it.’

Hearts now look set to drop into the Europa League, where they would face either Benfica or St Gallen in the third qualifying round, but Vrancken insists he hasn’t given up hope of overseeing a dramatic comeback in the return leg against Sturm Graz at Tynecastle next Tuesday.

‘You have to believe it,’ he said. ‘Especially at Tynecastle with the support of our fans. The ones who were here tonight were amazing, even with this result.

‘So we have go full out next week. If we are more efficient in the first half, then you never know. We could score some goals and there could be magic there. In this scenario, we still have to believe it.'

Sports.title: Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters
Sports.content:
Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters

Wouter Vrancken describes the style of play he likes to instil in his teams as ‘organised chaos’.

On a truly calamitous night in southern Austria, it was quite simply a disorganised disaster as the Belgian coach saw his Hearts tenure get off to the worst possible start.

It was all risk and no reward for the Gorgie club as Sturm Graz took an iron grip on this Champions League second qualifying round tie.

Defensively, Hearts were an absolute mess as Graz captain Jon Stankovic’s fourth minute opener was followed by a flurry of three goals in a torrid nine-minute spell early in the second half.

Barring a remarkable turnaround at Tynecastle next Tuesday night, Hearts will be dropping down into the Europa League qualifiers where it won’t get much easier for Vrancken.

The 47-year-old clearly needs time to bed his ideas in but will quickly find himself under serious pressure unless he restores some of the defensive discipline which was the hallmark of Hearts’ effectiveness under Derek McInnes last season.

Vrancken is left with questions to answer following a 4-0 hammering in Austria

It had been just 68 days since they lost out on the Premiership title in such agonising circumstances at Celtic Park and amid the pain experienced by club and supporters that afternoon, it was easy to lose sight of the fact they had still secured Champions League participation for the first time in 20 years.

Despite all of the close season upheaval at Tynecastle, with the departures of manager McInnes and key playing duo Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin to Rangers, new boss Vrancken relied on as many established squad members as possible for his opening night in the job.

Only two of Hearts new signings - defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott and winger Calvin Miller - were in the starting line-up named by Vrancken.

If he was looking to establish some early stability, however, Vrancken instead suffered disruption with the cheap and early concession of Sturm Graz’s opener.

It was Hearts who seemed to have made the brighter start, Christian Borchgrevink firing a shot over after Graz keeper Daniil Khudiakov unconvincingly palmed out Harry Milne’s low cross in the opening minute.

That sign of encouragement for the travelling fans was wiped out as Hearts completely switched off at the back when Jeyland Mitchell launched a long throw into their penalty area from the left. Jamie McCart was caught on his heels as Stankovic rose to guide a simple close range header beyond Alexander Schwolow.

The expansive and pacy attacking style of play Vrancken is renowned for was certainly evident but while Hearts looked good in possession, they remained wide open at the back.

Stankovic celebrates after Sturm Graz go 1-0 up inside four minutes

Graz missed a glaring opportunity to double their lead in the 10th minute when Simon Seidl’s corner was flicked on by Stankovic before Seedy Jatta hit a post with a free header from inside the six yard box.

When Schwolow had to react smartly to keep out a deflected shot from Jacob Hodl, there was a danger of the tie running away from Hearts.

They carved out plenty of menacing opportunities of their own, however, against a Graz defence which also appeared vulnerable.

After Claudio Braga had a low shot held by Khudiakov, Hearts should have equalised in the 25th minute. Oisin McEntee’s surging run carved a path into the Graz penalty area and the Irish midfielder showed great awareness to pick out Pierre Landry Kabore with his cutback.

It was a bread and butter chance for the big striker but with only Khudiakov to beat, he steered his shot straight into the grateful arms of the Russian keeper.

Graz went straight up the other end and Fagan-Walcott spared the blushes of his central defensive partner McCart who had played Jatta onside. The Norwegian striker looked certain to score until Fagan-Walcott slid in to make a brilliant block.

New arrival Guendouz is left frustrated after failing to make an impact

Neither side were willing to resort to a cautious approach as the contest continued to ebb and flow. Hearts wasted their best chance yet to level matters in the 34th minute. Braga won the ball high up the pitch and slid it to Alexandros Kyziridis who was unmarked inside the box.

It was the definition of a sitter but the Greek winger inexplicably sidefooted his shot wide of Khudiakov’s left hand post.

There was an anxious moment for Hearts six minutes before half-time when Hungarian referee Gergo Bogar pointed to the spot after Milne had slid in to block a shot from Szymon Wlodarczyk. While the ball hit the full-back’s arm, it did so only after bouncing up off his leg and a VAR review correctly saw the decision overturned.

Hearts’ start to the second half was the stuff of nightmares as Graz ran riot. The visitors were undone by another simple set piece when Mitchell had a free back post run to head home half-time sub Otar Kiteishvili’s corner from the left in the 50th minute.

Three minutes later, it was 3-0 when teenager Luca Weinhandl’s deflected shot beat Schwolow after Hearts made a mess of several chances to clear the danger.

They were carved wide open again in the 59th minute as Jurgen Heil played a one-two with Weinhandl on the right of the box before slamming the ball home.

Vrancken made a raft of changes in the closing half hour but Tom Renaud’s shot over was the closest Hearts came to pulling a goal back and perhaps giving them a sliver of hope for the second leg.

As it is, their long-awaited return to the Champions League looks as good as over.

Sports.title: West Ham accept £60m bid from Al-Hilal for Crysencio Summerville... with Premier League clubs now unlikely to compete at that price
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long-term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, Netherlands international Summerville was on Manchester United's radar and they held exploratory talks with West Ham.

Summerville joined the Hammers from Leeds for £25m in the summer of 2024 and scored eight goals in 56 games for the club but was unable to help them avoid relegation to the Championship last season.

West Ham are still looking to offload Jean-Clair Todibo, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Alphonse Areola, Edson Alvarez and Niclas Fullkrug.

Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville

With Aston Villa progressing on Alejandro Garnacho talks, Roma are now likely to look at RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, who also figured lower down on Arsenal's list, and his Norway compatriot Andreas Schjelderup at Benfica. Diego Moreira at Strasbourg has also been floated.

Sports.title: World Cup star Vinicius Jr packs on the PDA with his stunning girlfriend in Rio de Janeiro as he celebrates chin surgery success on lavish vacation
Sports.content:
World Cup star Vinicius Jr packs on the PDA with his stunning girlfriend in Rio de Janeiro as he celebrates chin surgery success on lavish vacation

Fresh off a stunning surgical procedure that altered his face, Brazilian football star Vinicius Junior was seen enjoying time with his girlfriend after an early World Cup exit.

The Real Madrid man was out in the sun at Reserva Beach in Rio de Janeiro with his on-and-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

Cameras captured an intimate moment between the two as Fonseca leaned in and planted a kiss on the footballer.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer.

Fonseca and her man continued to enjoy the sun as they relaxed before what should be a lengthy football season.

Real Madrid and Brazil star Vinicius Junior spent time on the beach with his girlfriend

A number of photos of the 26-year-old appearing unrecognizable after the op have gone viral on social media, with fans blown away by his remarkable transformation.

Vinicius posed alongside Dr. Alessandro Alarcao, who performed the surgery in Goiania, in another picture that has emerged online.

He underwent the procedure, which 'uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour', to add more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it during the World Cup.

And it seems like the Madrid player is happy with his dramatic new look, as he is all smiles in all of the post-op photos that have surfaced.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer

The pair remained close just hours after photos emerged of Vinicius' new look

The Brazil superstar looks completely different after undergoing chin harmonization surgery

🚨 Vini Jr at the clinic after his chin harmonization surgery. pic.twitter.com/WOq8OC0fgs — Madrid Zone (@theMadridZone) July 20, 2026

Fans were left astonished by the effect of the surgery on social media, with one writing: 'My brain can't wrap itself around the fact that this is Vini Jr. now, I swear'.

Another joked: 'I'll not believe this until I see him coming out to play a match looking like this'.

'MANNNN WHO THE F*** IS THAT,' a third said in bewilderment.

'Oh my God I don’t even recognize him,' a fourth commented.

While another user put: 'Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself'.

Vinicius and Brazil endured a frustrating World Cup before being eliminated by Norway at the last-16 stage.

Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Sqhnd3M0bX — Anabella💙❤️ (@AnabellaMarvy) July 21, 2026

Vinicius has added more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it online

He and Brazil were dumped out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage after a 2-1 loss to Norway

After finishing top of Group C, despite looking unconvincing in their opening draw against Morocco, they snatched a dramatic 96th-minute win over Japan in the last 32 after flattering to deceive again.

Carlo Ancelotti's men were then outclassed by Norway in New Jersey, with Erling Haaland's late double putting them out of sight before Neymar scored a consolation from the penalty spot with one of the last kicks of the game.

It wasn't a disastrous tournament for Vinicius from an individual standpoint, nevertheless, after he scored four goals before Brazil's exit.

Once his post-World Cup break is over, he will return to Madrid to begin preseason training ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers completes record move to Chelsea, West Ham agree £60m fee to sell Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal and Ipswich have £10m bid for Daizen Maeda accepted by Celtic: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea complete record Rogers deal

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of Morgan Rogers for a club-record £117m - which also makes him the most expensive British player of all time.

They have also had a £64m move for Alex Scott rejected by Bournemouth, who insist he is not for sale.

For more on this story click HERE

Morgan Rogers seals his £117m move to Chelsea in a deal announced at 9.45pm tonight

Toffees chew over Dewsbury

Everton are taking a look at Bristol Rovers prodigy Ollie Dewsbury.

The 18-year-old has also attracted attention from Arsenal and Fulham but is training with Everton ahead of a possible move.

Dewsbury became the youngest player to represent League Two Rovers in the FA Cup when he made his senior debut against Whitby Town in November 2023. Aged just 15 at the time, it made him the second youngest player to represent the club he has been at since the age of seven.

Palace still in for Matsima

Crystal Palace still working on Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima as a centre back option.

Daily Mail Sport last week reported their interest in the 6ft 4in defender, who has played for France at the Olympics.

Chrislain Matsima battles with Florian Wirtz before the Leverkusen star's move to Liverpool

Welcome (back) to Hull! Zambrano's a Tiger again

Hull City have confirmed the signing of Ecuadorian midfielder Oscar Zambrano from Maribor for an undisclosed fee.

The 22-year-old was on loan at Hull in 2024-25. He has signed a four-year contract, with the club holding an option to extend by a further 12 months.

Fulham set to bid £24m for Saint Shea

Fulham are preparing a £24million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Leeds United have so far fallen short of Southampton's demands for the Northern Ireland international with the Championship side holding out for £25million plus add-ons.

Leeds have made three proposals with add-ons but with agreement still to be found, Fulham are ready to make their move.

Manager Alvaro Arbeloa is on board with bringing in the 22-year-old who started out at Manchester City and talks are expected to advance.

Charles scored the winning goal against Middlesbrough which looked to have secured their place in the play-off final against Hull City only for Spygate to end their season abruptly.

He was left out of their squad to face Eastleigh in a friendly at the weekend however as he had been afforded more time off after being involved in international friendlies for Northern Ireland.

Shea Charles' goal against Boro looked to have sent Saints to Wembley before they were expelled for the Spygate scandal

Sutton send for City's Spike

Manchester City goalkeeper Spike Brits has joined National League side Sutton United on a season-long loan.

The 19-year-old, an England U18 international, has been at City since 2023 when they brought him in from AFC Wimbledon's academy.

Hull could throw a line for Fisher

Hull are keen on Norwich City right-back Kellen Fisher, 22, but have yet to make a formal bid.

Norwich remain determined to hold onto their first-choice right back this summer despite interest from Premier League sides.

Kellen Fisher competes with Fulham's Willian back in 2023

Forest set to offer £32m for Sporting's Diomande

Nottingham Forest are advancing in their talks for Sporting Lisbon defender Ousmane Diomande.

The centre back was a target for Oliver Glasner at Crystal Palace and the Ivory Coast international is open to moving to the Premier League.

Sources in Portugal say Sporting are pushing for £42million for the centre-back amid interest from AC Milan, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Leeds United. Forest are understood to be offering £32m. However, it is understood the other Premier League sides are yet to step up their interest.

Forest are light in central defence with Murillo returning from injury and interest building in Jair Cunha. They have signed Xaver Schlager and are ready to offer over £45m for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall.

£60m deal agreed for Summerville

Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

For more on this story click HERE

Crysencio Summerville has been a target for several clubs this summer

Ipswich's £10m Daizen bid does trick

Ipswich Town have had a £10m bid for Celtic’s Daizen Maeda accepted. A deal worth £8m up front and £2m in add-ons has been agreed in principle.

Earlier this month the forward confirmed his wish to move to England .

‘Since I went to Celtic, I became interested in the Premier League,’ he told Japanese YouTube show Pivot. ‘I started watching a lot of Premier League games. I have a strong desire to play in the Premier League.'

The Tractor Boys have also completed their deal for Leicester winger Abdul Fatawu today, with manager Gary O'Neil saying of the 22-year-old: 'Abdul is a young player who has already gained good experience in the game and we’re excited to have him with us.

'He has strong physical and technical attributes, is comfortable on the ball and can test the opposition in one-on-one situations, so will provide us with good options within the squad.

'Having represented his country at the World Cup this summer, I know he is now looking forward to getting to work ahead of the Premier League season.'

Daizen Maeda played a big role for Japan at the World Cup this summer

Villa likely to seal deal for Garnacho

Aston Villa are expected to land Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell in percentage.

Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

PFA free agent squad in action tonight

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Around 48 players have now joined the PFA pre-season camp where they train and play a series of friendlies to showcase their availability to clubs over the summer.

Former Manchester United and Port Vale keeper Ben Amos and ex-Ipswich Town striker Connor Wickham are among a growing band of players looking to earn contracts elsewhere.

Another friendly is planned at Tranmere Rovers on Friday.

The games can be viewed on the PFA's live YouTube stream.

Spurs agree to sell Lankshear to Middlesbrough

Tottenham have agreed to sell Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £14million potentially rising to £20m with add-ons.

There is also a 20 per cent sell on clause and Spurs have matching rights on any bids from other clubs in the future.

Striker Lankshear, 21, who was on loan at Oxford United last season, is expected for a medical later today.

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.

BOBBY MANZI AND CHRIS WHEELER
