World.title: Dubai OFWs pay it forward with scholarships for Filipinos back home
World.content:
Marilyn Flores Castro, a former OFW who now owns a group of companies, and Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants - Dubai headed by Lyndon Magsino are currently supporting a total of 30 scholars

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates – A group of accountants and a Filipina who runs a group of companies here have separately launched scholarship programs that have so far benefited a total of 30 students in the Philippines.

“I myself was a product of scholarship programs in high school and college in the Philippines, so it was my dream to also help students who wanted to finish their studies but didn’t have the financial means to do so,” Marilyn Flores Castro told Rappler in Filipino.

Castro, who started out in Dubai as an overseas Filipino worker (OFW), is now the owner of Pinas Group of Companies, which runs six diverse enterprises that grew from an original balikbayan box enterprise launched in 2014.

SPONSOR. Pinas Cargo Group of Companies CEO Marilyn Flores Castro says she herself finished her studies because of the generosity of sponsors. PCG photo

“I really wanted to study and have a diploma, but my parents didn’t have the means to support my and my siblings’ studies. We were poor. I finished high school on scholarships, while in college I got help from a philantrophist who helped poor students like who were determined to finish schooling,” she added.

Castro finished financial and management accounting at Holy Angel University in Angeles City, Pampanga.

Now that she’s a businesswoman herself, Castro said, “God has given me the opportunity help others and share the blessings He has provided.”

Launched in 2018, her Pinas Cargo Scholarship Program currently supports 25 scholars across different countries. Of these, 22 scholars are pursuing their studies in the Philippines, one in the United Arab Emirates, one in Pakistan, and one in Africa. The program has had six Filipino college graduates, the latest being Jhimton Sasota (left), who completed computer engineering at the Bicol University in Polangui, Albay.

Meanwhile, the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants – Dubai (PICPA-Dubai) has also launched a scholarship program for children enabling them to finish K-12.

At least five children are beneficiaries of the program and five more are being planned for 2026.

It was a “simple yet meaningful missions to help children from less fortunate families in the Philippines pursue their education and build a brighter future,” said PICPA-Dubai founder and head, Lyndon Magsino.

GIVING BACK. Lyndon Magsino founded and heads the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountant-Dubai, which sponsors K-12 scholars. PICPA photo

“As members of PICPA-Dubai have been blessed with opportunities to grow professionally and personally, we believe it is our responsibility to give back to our communities. This scholarship program is our humble way of becoming a channel of hope, opportunity, and lasting impact in the lives of others,” he added.

The group selects “children from families facing genuine financial hardship, those who simply needed an opportunity to continue their education,” Magsino said. The selection entails “recommendations from barangay captains and school principals.”

ACHIEVER. Aljur Joseph Ocop is a scholar of the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountant-Dubai. PICPA photo

Many of the five beneficiaries “were already at risk of becoming, or had become, out-of-school youth,” said Magsino.

The scholarship fund is made possible through contributions from PICPA-Dubai members, event participants, sponsors, partners, and donors. – Rappler.com

World.title: ‘No response’ from ASEAN ministers on Ayungin clash; PH, China set to meet
World.content:
The lack of a response is because the Philippines and China are still 'discussing' the issue, says Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro

MANILA, Philippines – Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said on Tuesday, July 21, she raised a recent confrontation between Chinese and Filipino personnel at Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal with her counterparts in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), but they “did not respond.”

“I was the one who presented it as part of the discussion… but the foreign ministers did not respond to that position that I made because I think everything is still being discussed between the two parties,” said Lazaro in a huddle with media late Tuesday, following the retreat session between ASEAN foreign ministers in Manila.

On July 20, or just as foreign ministers from all over the bloc began holding high-level meetings in Manila, a Filipino soldier sustained a gash after the China Coast Guard (CCG) hit him with a “wooden baton,” according to the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

The confrontation took place just over 20 yards from the BRP Sierra Madre, an active-service warship that was run aground at Ayungin Shoal in 1999 and serves as a Philippine military outpost.

It was the first major confrontation between China and the Philippines in the South China Sea since July 2024, when the China Coast Guard rammed a Philippine boat moored to the Sierra Madre during a resupply mission, severing a Filipino soldier’s thumb.

Lazaro is schedule to meet separately with her counterparts from the United States and China — US State Secretary Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi — who are both in Manila for the ASEAN meetings.

The retreat was the second of two meetings the foreign ministers were scheduled to attend on July 21. In ASEAN, the plenary is the more formal gathering, typically devoted to reviewing progress on previously agreed goals and resulting in the issuance of a joint statement. A retreat, meanwhile, is considered a more “informal” session where more sensitive subjects, such as pressing geopolitical and regional issues, are discussed.

“There was a statement, of course, made on the South China Sea by me and the other various ministers but I think what was really emphatic about was the Code of Conduct (COC). Almost all have really focused themselves on the development that has happened in the COC between ASEAN and China,” added Lazaro.

The Philippines, as ASEAN chair, hopes to conclude negotiations on a code of conduct (COC) before its turn ends. The COC is intended to set rules for ASEAN and China to follow to avoid an escalation of tensions in the South China Sea. Several ASEAN members, including the Philippines, are claimants in the South China Sea. Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea as its territory, even if international law says this cannot be the case.

On July 21, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. summoned to Malacañang Chinese ambassador Jing Quan over the Ayungin Shoal incident.

Tensions between the two countries have been steadily rising in the past month. Beijing sanctioned Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. over his statements on China, making him the second Marcos Cabinet member to be under sanction. Former senator Francis Tolentino, Marcos’ new labor chief, was sanctioned in 2025 after his Senate term expired.

Various government agencies, including the Department of Foreign Affairs led by Lazaro, also criticized China after state-run China Daily released a video, widely seen as racist, that portrayed the Philippines as a monkey in its critique of the landmark 2016 arbitral award. – Rappler.com

World.title: Hearsay? Defense questions Matibag’s knowledge of Sara Duterte’s ‘threats’
World.content:
MATIBAG. National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag testifies in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines – The defense team of Sara Duterte centered its cross-examination on Tuesday, July 21, by pounding on National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag’s lack of personal knowledge of some aspects of the NBI’s probe into the Vice President’s alleged grave threats.

During his cross-examination, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan laid out the NBI director’s lack of personal knowledge by asking him a series of queries. First, Vinluan asked Matibag about the 10 subpoenas issued to the personalities who attended Duterte’s 2024 press conference, where she allegedly threatened President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Each time Matibag said he lacked personal knowledge of a specific document flashed on the screen, the defense put an “X” emoji on it.

The NBI director said he was also not the signatory to the NBI subpoenas because he was not yet appointed at the time.

“The witness already testified that he has no personal knowledge about the first investigation. And all his testimonies will be based only on the records existing in the NBI,” lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro interjected during the trial.

Matibag explained on Tuesday that the NBI probe has two parts. The first was the investigation right after the November 2024 press conference under a different NBI head. The second probe, meanwhile, refers to the special task force created by Matibag’s Administrative Order No. 11 last April.

Vinluan later went straight to his point: witnesses can only testify to the information they have personal knowledge of. During the trial, he asked Matibag about the rule on the limitations of testimony, stating Section 22 of Rule 130 of the amended rules on evidence.

“A witness can testify only to those facts which he or she knows of his or her personal knowledge; that is, which are derived from his or her own perception,” the provision stated.

The defense’s point was that Matibag only has personal knowledge so far as the second probe is concerned.

“Ang sinasabi natin is, pagdating do’n sa unang investigation na wala siyang personal knowledge, ‘yon po ay tinatawag nating hearsay. So, ibig sabihin, wala kang personal na kaalaman kasi hindi ka na-involve doon sa investigasyon na ‘yon,” defense spokesperson and counsel Michael Poa told reporters in a briefing.

(What we are saying is, in terms of the first investigation, which he has no personal knowledge of, that’s hearsay. This means a person has no personal knowledge because that person was not involved in the investigation.)

Play Video

Testing Matibag’s credibility, ‘bias’

Similar to past impeachment trials, the defense team cast doubt on Matibag by testing his credibility and supposed bias.

“Ang point namin talaga is to test the credibility, test kung may bias man o wala,” Poa said. “We were really just testing the credibility at kung may personal bias ‘yong witness because that will, syempre, affect ‘yong integrity ng kaniyang mga naging testimonya or at least ‘yong pagsasagawa ng imbestigasyon.”

(Our point is to test the credibility, test if there’s bias or none. We were really just testing the credibility, and if the witness has personal bias, that will affect the integrity of his testimony or his conduct of investigation.)

The defense also touched on Matibag’s personal life, specifically on his incident with friend Mel Sabio.

Last May, Matibag was in hot water after his conversation with his friend leaked. In the viral video, Matibag was arguing with Sabio over the phone, and, at one point, the NBI director could be heard allegedly threatening to harm his friend.

However, Matibag and Sabio have already reconciled after the incident.

As to the alleged bias, the defense also highlighted that Matibag’s wife, Laguna 1st District Representative Ann Matibag, is among the lawmakers who backed the articles of impeachment against Duterte.

Vinluan also presented Matibag’s opinion article, “Inday Sara, The Bratinella,” which depicted the Vice President as a brat.

“Yes, my wife is one of the endorsers of the impeachment,” Matibag said during the trial.

“My decision to be a witness is by virtue of a subpoena issued by the honorable court and by invitation of the committee on justice, the prosecution. However, the job of my wife as a legislator is totally detached from me being the director of the National Bureau of Investigation,” he further explained.

Play Video

“We meant no offense, and I hope none was taken by Director Matibag. We respect that, except that in cross-examinations, you really have to test not just the credibility but also bias,” Poa said in a mix of English and Filipino.

Objecting to Lascañas’ affidavit

The prosecution asked Matibag to read portions of self-confessed Davao Death Squad member Arturo Lascañas’ affidavit, which mentioned the Vice President. This affidavit has been submitted to the International Criminal Court as part of the crimes against humanity case against Duterte’s father, former president Rodrigo Duterte.

Lascañas named the Vice President over five times in his affidavit. There, he claimed that they had allegedly received kill orders from the former president, then later, from Sara as Davao City mayor.

In another instance, Lascañas claimed that an abduction operation allegedly ordered by Sara had been relayed to him at one point.

For the defense, Matibag’s reading of the document during the trial was “highly improper.”

“We already allowed the witness [to] at least identify this document. But as to the fact that he is allowed to read even portions thereof, he’s not the author of this affidavit. And as to the truth or falsity thereof, [he’s] incompetent to testify on that. And it…already violates the rights of our client because she’s being prejudiced by the reading of this affidavit,” Vinluan explained.

The impeachment court allowed the defense’s motion to continue its cross-examination of Matibag on Wednesday, July 22, to give them more time to study the Lascañas document. – Rappler.com

World.title: Barangay health workers appeal to Marcos: Revive Magna Carta as priority bill
World.content:
LONG-STANDING PLEA. Barangay health workers submit an appeal letter to Malacañang to seek the passage of their own Magna Carta, July 21, 2026.

They hope President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. would include the proposed Magna Carta of Barangay Health Workers in his upcoming State of the Nation Address on July 27

MANILA, Philippines – Barangay health workers (BHWs) from various cities in Metro Manila submitted an appeal letter to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday, July 21, to reiterate their calls for a Magna Carta ahead of his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA).

Representatives of the National Confederation of Barangay Health Workers of the Philippines (NCBHWP) and labor group UNI Global Union–Philippine Liaison Council personally delivered their letter to Malacañang, calling for the proposed Magna Carta of BHWs to be restored as a priority legislative measure.

“For more than four decades, BHWs have waited for the enactment of a Magna Carta that would uphold and protect our rights,” they wrote in the letter.

APPEAL. The first page of the National Confederation of Barangay Health Workers of the Philippines and UNI Global Union–Philippine Liaison Council’s appeal letter addressed to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Photo by Eirene Manatlao/Rappler

Myrna Gaite, a barangay health worker and president of the BHW Federation of the National Capital Region, recounted how some of her colleagues have died without ever receiving better compensation.

“Ako, 40 years in service na ako. Boluntaryo ako, nagsimula sa wala…. Pinapanalangin ng bawat barangay health worker na magkaroon ng katugunan ang Magna Carta dahil doon napapaloob ang lahat ng mga benepisyo para sa mga BHW,” Gaite said.

(I’ve been in service for 40 years. I was a volunteer who started with nothing. Every barangay health worker is praying for the Magna Carta to be realized, as it encompasses all benefits for BHWs.)

The Marcos administration previously included the proposed Magna Carta of BHWs as a priority measure of the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council in 2023.

The bill was nearing approval before the 19th Congress ended, but failed when the House of Representatives withdrew its version’s transmittal.

“In 2023, the President gave renewed hope to hundreds of thousands of BHWs when he publicly committed to supporting our Magna Carta. Today, BHWs are humbly appealing to the President to fulfill his promise,” NCBHWP president Khonan Cerial said.

BHWs, the primary healthcare providers at the barangay level, are left with a heavy workload and additional responsibilities not in their job description, all while being compensated poorly as volunteers.

The Magna Carta bill at the Senate, which has been approved on second reading as of writing, promises to institutionalize the employment of BHWs and give them permanent government positions. Instead of just honoraria and flexible benefits, they would be entitled to receive pay equivalent to Salary Grade 1.

Lyma Rico, Marikina BHW Federation president, said: “Ito na ang pagkakataon ng barangay health workers na maipasa ang Magna Carta. Sa tagal-tagal na lumipas na panahon, hindi man lang maipasa. Siguro ito na ‘yung pagkakataon na ibigay niya sa amin ito.”

(This is the opportunity for the Magna Carta of BHWs to be finally enacted into law. It has languished for so long. Perhaps the President will now grant our plea.)

Marcos is set to deliver his fifth SONA on Monday, July 27. – Rappler.com

World.title: Future Kiyapo? Incoming LPA has high chance of becoming tropical depression
World.content:
LPA. Satellite image of the low pressure area outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of July 21, 2026, 3 pm.

The low pressure area might enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Wednesday, July 22

MANILA, Philippines – A low pressure area (LPA) outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) has a high chance of developing into a tropical depression within 24 hours, the weather bureau said on Tuesday afternoon, July 21.

The LPA had formed outside PAR on Monday, July 20. As of 3 pm on Tuesday, it was located 1,505 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said the LPA might enter PAR within 12 to 24 hours, or by Wednesday, July 22.

If it becomes a tropical cyclone inside PAR or enters PAR as a tropical cyclone, it would be given the local name Kiyapo — the Filipino word for water cabbage or water lettuce. Manila’s Quiapo district got its name from this plant.

The potential Kiyapo would be the Philippines’ 11th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the fourth for July.

PAGASA Weather Specialist Benison Estareja said the incoming weather disturbance could reach tropical storm intensity. In this scenario, the highest possible tropical cyclone wind signal would be Signal No. 2.

Estareja added that the future Kiyapo could move toward Northern Luzon on Friday, July 24, or Saturday, July 25. This means Northern Luzon and even Central Luzon may be directly affected during the second half of the week.

For now, the trough or extension of the LPA could bring scattered rain and thunderstorms to Eastern Visayas on Tuesday evening.

PAGASA advised the public to regularly monitor updates on the potential tropical cyclone as forecasts can still change.

The weather bureau is also warning the public to watch out for rain from the southwest monsoon or habagat, especially on the western side of the country.

Mindanao, Western Visayas, the Negros Island Region, Central Visayas, and Palawan are seeing scattered rain and thunderstorms due to the southwest monsoon on Tuesday evening. At the moment, Metro Manila only has localized thunderstorms, which are not linked to the southwest monsoon.

Rain from the southwest monsoon is likely to worsen in the coming days, with PAGASA releasing the following outlook at 5 pm on Tuesday:

Wednesday afternoon, July 22, to Thursday afternoon, July 23

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 millimeters): Maguindanao del Norte, Sultan Kudarat, Sarangani

Thursday afternoon, July 23, to Friday afternoon, July 24

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Negros Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Sultan Kudarat

Floods and landslides are possible. – Rappler.com

World.title: Iranian forces target Bahrain and Kuwait after US hits Iran’s south
World.content:
IRAN TARGET. Military equipment targeted at an unknown location, during what US Central Command (CENTCOM) says are strikes on Iran, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on July 20, 2026.

Despite the escalating cycle of attacks that has all but wrecked an interim peace agreement signed in June, signs that Tehran and Washington want to resume diplomacy keep oil prices in check

DUBAI, UAE – US forces bombed targets in southern Iran overnight after President Donald Trump said Tehran would pay dearly for the deaths of American soldiers, while Iran targeted US sites in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan and a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

The exchanges came a day after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said they would impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, opening a potential new front in the war and raising the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf.

Despite the escalating cycle of attacks that has all but wrecked an interim peace agreement signed last month, signs that Tehran and Washington want to resume diplomacy kept oil prices in check.

US Central Command said it had completed its latest round of strikes on Iran, saying it hit Iranian military command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems.

Explosions were heard around the city of Shiraz in southern Iran, while Konarak and Chabahar on the southern coast also came under attack, according to state media.

Iran responded with renewed attacks across the Gulf, where recent strikes on desalination facilities have raised concerns about water shortages and underscored the growing threat to civilian infrastructure.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted infrastructure in Bahrain belonging to US tech company Amazon in retaliation for what they described as a US strike on the construction site of Iran’s planned Darkhovin nuclear power plant.

Iranian state media reported that Iranian forces also targeted accommodation facilities used by US military personnel at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa Air Base. There was no immediate comment from the US military, Bahrain or Amazon on the reported incidents, which Reuters was unable to verify.

The Iranian army said it launched drone attacks against three US military bases in Kuwait on Tuesday. The Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a US military site in Jordan, and Jordan said its forces intercepted and destroyed five Iranian drones.

Tankers struck

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Tuesday a tanker in the strait reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

Also on Tuesday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers had caught fire after explosions while attempting to transit the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz. It was not immediately clear when those incidents took place.

Iran had been pressing the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the US continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure — putting two of the world’s most vital energy arteries at risk.

A full closure of Bab el-Mandeb would reduce global oil supply by 7% as it would leave most Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the huge cut to oil flows from the war in the Gulf, which has already reduced shipments by 10% of global supply.

After the Houthis announced their blockade, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it began implementing protection measures for its ships moving through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Oil markets weighed the threat to shipping against reports of diplomatic efforts to contain the conflict, with benchmark Brent crude prices easing slightly in early trading.

Diplomatic push to restore ceasefire

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday that Tehran had received a proposal from mediators for a 10-day ceasefire in efforts to salvage the interim deal, intended to pave the way to a lasting agreement to end the war that began on February 28 with US-Israeli attacks on Iran.

Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni had asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in the conflict. He later arrived in Islamabad for further talks.

The latest phase of fighting has proved to be among the deadliest of the conflict for US forces. US troop deaths rose to 17 over the weekend.

Trump, under mounting pressure at home over rising gasoline prices since the war began, said the latest US strikes on Iran were honoring the deaths of American service members.

“Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over! This directive has been passed on to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine, and every Leader in the Military,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday.

The war has killed thousands of people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. Parts of Lebanon remain under Israeli occupation following attacks on Israel by Hezbollah fighters, who said they were acting in solidarity with Tehran.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun is due to meet Trump at the White House on Tuesday to present a plan on how to disarm Iran-aligned Hezbollah and secure an Israeli withdrawal. – Rappler.com

World.title: Baguio garbage fee hike to finance waste services, Magalong says
World.content:
Workers load sacks of garbage onto a truck as part of the daily trash collection in downtown Baguio. — Photo by Vincent Cabreza

BAGUIO CITY — Mayor Benjamin Magalong defended the Baguio City council’s approval last week of an ordinance increasing household garbage collection fees, saying the adjustment has long been overdue and would sustain the city’s waste management services.

In a video posted by the Baguio City Public Information Office on July 21, the mayor said the city government could no longer maintain quality garbage collection under the existing fee structure of P20 monthly payments per household while spending about P200 million annually to subsidize collection and shipment of non-recyclable trash to commercial landfills outside the city.

“You cannot expect us to deliver excellent garbage collection when the garbage fee has not increased in more than 20 years,” the mayor said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Baguio spends up to P200M yearly to haul residual waste

Magalong said the ordinance still requires his signature before it takes effect.

Magalong said many first and second-class municipalities (which generate incomes of more than P200 million) have been imposing P70 to P80 monthly garbage fees without the waste management burdens shouldered by Baguio.

The city government permanently shut down its only open dump at Barangay Irisan in 2012 and turned it into an ecological park following a 2011 fatal trash slide that prompted the Catholoc clergy, residents of Baguio, neighboring Tuba town in Benguet to seek and win a permanent environmental protection order from the Court of Appeals.

A landfill option was discarded because no area within Baguio’s terrain is suited for this waste management system so hauling trash out of the city has been the only way to manage waste.

Article continues after this 

“We have to fix the system if we want to implement a comprehensive solid waste management plan,” Magalong said in the video.

READ: Baguio to require waste plans for public events

Article continues after this 

Under the approved ordinance, households served by the city’s garbage collection system will pay P75 per month, or P900 annually. Residents who pay the full year’s fee on or before April 20 may avail themselves of a 10-percent discount, reducing the annual payment to P810.

The ordinance also updates garbage fees for commercial, institutional and industrial establishments. Dormitories, boarding houses, apartments, hostels, inns and transient houses will pay between P400 to P1,000 every month based on bed capacity, while hotels will be charged P600 to P1,200 based on the number of rooms they operate.

Hospitals, restaurants, bars, banks, offices, schools, transportation terminals, parking areas, public markets and other businesses will also pay revised garbage fees based on their size, capacity or number of employees.

Businesses operating an additional line of business in the same establishment will pay an additional garbage fee equivalent to 25 percent of the rate imposed on their principal business.

The ordinance authorizes the City Treasurer to deputize barangay treasurers to collect household garbage fees. Barangays will receive 50 percent of the collections from their constituents, with incentives that could raise their share to 75 percent if they achieve full collection efficiency.

Late payments will be subject to a 25-percent surcharge and 2-percent monthly interest, while garbage fees will automatically increase by 10 percent every three years beginning in 2027, subject to periodic review by the city council.

The measure also imposes penalties for improper waste disposal, including a warning for the first offense, a P1,500 fine for the second offense and a P3,000 fine for the third and succeeding offenses.

World.title: Adiong: Those in conflict-hit areas won’t wait for threats to be bullets
World.content:
Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong — Photo from Cong. Zia Alonto Adiong/Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — How important is it that the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) investigated Vice President Sara Duterte’s threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his relatives?

According to Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, any person like him who hails from conflict-stricken areas would think that it was necessary to probe any threat before they even turn into bullets.

Alonto Adiong said this after members of the prosecution team were asked if they are concerned that NBI Director Melvin Matibag’s refusal to publicize the identities of people possibly contracted by Duterte weakens their case — and contributes to the defense’s claims that no hitman was hired.

Article continues after this 

“Are we concerned because the NBI has not named names, only that Director Matibag informed the court that there are already persons of interest that they would like to follow lead in terms of investigation ano? No, we are not concerned. What we are more concerned (about) is if the NBI had not stepped in and investigate the case,” Alonto Adiong said in a press briefing on Tuesday night.

READ: 4 years after siege, Marawi folk desperate to trek back home

“Why am I saying this? Having (been) raised in a community where we are all exposed to conflict, we cannot let the government sit down and wait until words become bullets,” he added.

Alonto Adiong hails from Mindanao, which over the past decades was rocked by violence due to the communist insurgency, separatist movements, and terrorist groups.

Lanao del Sur is also home to Marawi City, a vibrant Islamic City which was laid to siege by the terrorist Maute Group in May 2017. Intense fighting between military forces and Maute members lasted for five months, and left a large-scale humanitarian crisis with over 300,000 residents displaced.

Article continues after this 

According to Alonto Adiong, Duterte’s threats must not be set aside because had it been implemented, it would have resulted in instability and chaos within the country.

“That’s clearly a threat and this should not be set aside or simply disregarded. So I think it’s more concerning for the Filipino people if the NBI did not do anything,” he said.

Article continues after this 

“At least now, we have learned from the NBI Director that they are still on an ongoing case build-up, open investigation, and there are persons of interest proving that the grave threat is not just uttered in words but there was already that plan,” he added.

During the resumption of the impeachment trial, Matibag was presented by the prosecution to shed light on the NBI’s investigation of Duterte’s threats, which she made in an online press briefing on November 23, 2024.

In that briefing, Duterte was asked by a vlogger to take care as she may be in danger. The vice president then responded by urging people not to worry about her as she has already talked to a person about killing Marcos, his wife First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and his cousin former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez if she herself gets killed.

However, when asked to show documents pointing to the possible hitman contracted by Duterte, Matibag declined, saying that showing confidential information may hamper their continuing investigation.

READ:

The defense panel has maintained even before the impeachment trial that Duterte’s statements were part of free speech. However, several government officials and prosecutors believe it was a grave threat — regardless of whether or not the Vice President executed a contract with an assassin to kill the three.

READ: With or without contract to kill, VP made impeachable offense – lawmaker

Matibag is the third and last witness from the prosecution panel for Article IV of the Articles of Impeachment, or the allegation that deals with Duterte’s grave threats.

The prosecution intended to present several other witnesses, including Office of the Vice President chief-of-staff and Undersecretary Zuleika Lopez, but Luistro and counsel for the prosecution Lorna Kapunan announced during the second week of the trial that they will no longer call them.

READ: Prosec won’t call sheriff, reporters as witnesses in impeach trial anymore

According to Luistro and Kapunan, they believe they have established matters that the prosecution needs to sustain a conviction. /das

World.title: Cordillera inflation slows in June on lower gas prices
World.content:
Workers load vegetables onto a truck in Benguet. — Photo by Vincent Cabreza

BAGUIO CITY — Inflation in the summer capital and the rest of mountainous Cordillera again slowed down in June, sustaining a substantial drop in inflation back in May, due to the gradual decline in gas prices when a ceasefire and peace talks between the United States and Iran were still in place, the region’s chief statistician reported at a Friday (July 17) economic briefing.

Baguio inflation grew more slowly at 6.7 percent last month from 7 percent in May, while the Cordillera provinces of Benguet, Ifugao, Abra, Apayao, Kalinga and Mountain Province and this mountain city combined recorded a 6.5 percent inflation rate in June, down from 6.8 percent in May, said Aldrin Federico Bahit Jr, Cordillera senior statistician of the Philippine Statistics Authority.

The May inflation rate climbed down from a high 7.6 percent inflation rate in April.

Article continues after this 

READ: Cordillera inflation in May slows down to 6.8 percent

The primary drivers of a slowed down inflation in the summer capital were transport and food because diesel inflation rapidly declined to 25.8 percent rate in June from 46.7 percent rate in May, and as well as a similarly sharp drop for gasoline inflation to 38.5 percent last month following a high 47.9 percent rate in May.

Baguio typically has the more expensive costs for gas and diesel in the region despite its proximity to La Union fuel depots which is about an hour’s drive.

Many local economists are monitoring how renewed fighting in the now five-month long war on Iran would impact July inflation and the Cordillera economy.

Baguio is a tourist destination and an educational and business hub in this part of Luzon which relies heavily on travellers. Meanwhile, Benguet supplies 80 percent of the salad vegetable requirements of Manila and other provinces that need to be shipped down each day.

Article continues after this 

READ: Cordillera braces for worst as fuel shocks hike inflation

Throughout the Cordillera, declining fuel costs also brought inflation down. Diesel inflation for the mountain region dropped to 33.4 percent in June from a high of 53.4 percent in May. Gas inflation for the Cordillera was 40.3 percent last month from 49 percent in May. LPG (liquefied petroleum gas), which most households use, had an inflation rate of 41.8 percent in June from 50.9 percent in May.

Article continues after this 

Because June was also the start of the school year, PSA observed the slight rise in the costs of rice (7.5 percent inflation rate in June from 6.6 percent in May), while reflecting a general downgrade in costs covering rent and utilities (9.5 percent in June from 9.7 percent in May) and sustained inflation for clothing and footwear (2.1 percent in June from 2.1 percent in May).

Inflation for fish like bangus (milkfish) which is imported from coastline provinces like Pangasinan slid down to a rate of 88 percent in June from 9.4 percent in May. Vegetables like squash caused inflation for this sector to climb to 5.4 percent in June from 3.4 percent in May.

The cost of alcoholic beverages and tobacco grew to 6.9 percent in June from 6.3 percent in May, coinciding with the rise in inflation for restaurants and accommodation services associated with tourism to 8.3 percent in June from 8 percent in May.

Ifugao, home of the world heritage-enshrined rice terraces, reflected the lowest inflation (3.7 percent in June from 4.2 percent in May) among Cordillera provinces. Apayao, one of the country’s biosphere reserves, had the highest inflation in the Cordillera with a 15 percent rate in June from 14.5 in May. /das

World.title: Pagasa: LPA to bring rain, strong winds over N. Luzon
World.content:
Weather specialist Chenel Dominguez reports that a low-pressure area is forecast to bring heavy rains and strong gusts of wind over Northern Luzon as it approaches the country on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. — Screengrab from DOST-Pagasa/Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — A low-pressure area (LPA) is forecast to bring heavy rains and strong gusts of wind over Northern Luzon as it approaches the country, the state weather bureau said.

“As it (LPA) nears the landmass, we expect heavy rains and winds, especially in Northern Luzon,” Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) weather specialist Chenel Dominguez reported during a 5 a.m. weather advisory on Wednesday.

As of 3 a.m., the LPA was estimated 1,200 kilometers east of Southeastern Luzon. Once it develops into a tropical cyclone and enters the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) it will be given a domestic name Kiyapo, Dominguez said.

Article continues after this 

READ: LPA outside Pagasa has moderate chance of becoming typhoon – Pagasa

The LPA is expected to enter the PAR on Wednesday morning, moving generally northwestward. Dominguez said the weather disturbance could make landfall over Cagayan between Friday to Saturday.

“Its projected track is generally northwestward, potentially bringing it close to or making landfall in Cagayan, likely between Friday and Saturday,” Dominguez said.

She added that LPA could reach tropical storm category, with the highest wind signals being hoisted to signal number 2.

“In terms of intensity, we also expect it to reach tropical storm category, with the highest Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal to be raised being Signal No. 2,” Dominguez stated.

Article continues after this 

The trough of the LPA is expected to bring gloomy skies with scattered rains over Bicol Region and Eastern Visayas on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms are also expected to prevail over the following areas due to the southwest monsoon, or habagat, according to Pagasa.

Article continues after this 

Mindanao

Western Visayas

Negros Island Region

Central Visayas

Palawan

Pagasa issued a heavy rainfall advisory in the following areas, with 50 to 100 millimeters of rain forecast due to the habagat:

Maguindanao del Norte

Sultan Kudarat

Sarangani

Localized thunderstorms are likely to bring partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms over Manila and the rest of Luzon. /das

World.title: NBI chief: VP’s kill threat a nat’l security concern
World.content:
FINAL WITNESS ON ARTICLE IV NBI Director Melvin Matibag notes similarities between the October 2024 remarks of Vice President Sara Duterte about imagining herself cutting off President Marcos’ head (lower right photo), and Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte’s statement during the April 12 RAGE coalition rally (upper right), where he declared they wanted “only BBM’s head.” —Photos by Ñino Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel on Tuesday presented National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag as its final witness on Article IV of the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte, with the NBI chief testifying that the bureau no longer views Duterte’s controversial “kill” remarks against President Marcos as a mere threat but as a “serious, active and continuing” assassination plot that has become a national security concern.

“Our observation is that this is no longer merely a threat but a plan,” Matibag testified in Filipino. “We believe the Vice President announced her plan to kill the President of the Philippines, as well as the other individuals she said she wanted killed during her press conference.”

The defense, however, sought more time to complete its cross-examination on Wednesday before prosecutors could formally rest their case under Article IV, which accuses Duterte of culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust over her alleged threats against Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Article continues after this 

READ: NBI exec: Evidence points to Sara Duterte’s kill plot against Marcos

Appearing on the eighth day of the impeachment trial, Matibag said the NBI had elevated its investigation beyond the criminal complaints for grave threats and inciting to sedition pending before the Department of Justice by creating a special task force to examine what it considers an ongoing threat against the President.

Formed in April, the task force brings together investigators from the NBI’s Cybercrime and Transnational Crimes divisions to determine whether Duterte’s public statements reflected an actual conspiracy to assassinate the President.

READ: Threats vs president also threaten national security – NBI chief

Matibag said investigators reached that conclusion after analyzing Duterte’s Oct. 18, 2024 and Nov. 23, 2024 online press conferences, in which she spoke of wanting to cut off the President’s head and later declared she had instructed someone to kill Marcos, the first lady and Romualdez should she herself be assassinated.

Article continues after this 

Persons of interest

“It is clear from our open-source intelligence that the Vice President said she contracted someone to kill the President, and that person supposedly agreed,” Matibag said.

The NBI chief disclosed that investigators have identified several “persons of interest” who could lead authorities to the individual Duterte allegedly referred to in her November 2024 remarks.

Article continues after this 

“We have leads that we are pursuing. In fact, we have already identified persons of interest who may be able to identify the individual the Vice President spoke to. It is also possible that one of these persons of interest is the very person the Vice President spoke with,” Matibag said.

He refused to identify them, saying disclosure could compromise the ongoing investigation.

“I cannot disclose the identities of these persons of interest. It would violate their right to privacy and compromise an ongoing investigation,” Matibag said.

“For me, this is no longer really a threat but rather a confession of her plan to kill our President because she herself said, ‘I spoke to someone, and the person I spoke to agreed to kill the President,’” Matibag added.

Defense counsel Mark Vinluan asked that the statement be stricken from the record, arguing that Matibag was offering a legal conclusion. Presiding officer Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero allowed the answer to remain as part of the witness’ narration but instructed senator-judges not to treat it as a conclusion of law.

Possible conspiracy

Responding to questions from Sen. Bam Aquino, Matibag said he was “100 percent certain” Duterte had spoken to someone about carrying out the killing because “she herself revealed her plan” and said the person agreed.

He added that while the NBI has actionable intelligence indicating a continuing threat to the President’s life, it has no similar intelligence regarding any threat to Duterte.

Matibag also asserted that Duterte had the means to carry out the alleged plot because she was “well-connected” with military and police personnel and had access to money and firearms.

He testified that the NBI is also examining a possible conspiracy involving Duterte and her brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, after noting similarities in their public remarks about Marcos.

“It is noticeable that the threats against our President came from one family. Both are referring to the President’s head,” Matibag said. “That’s why we wondered if there was an accomplice or a conspiracy behind this incident.”

He said investigators considered Baste Duterte’s remarks during the April 12 RAGE coalition rally, where the mayor declared they wanted only Marcos’ “head,” and compared them with Sara Duterte’s October 2024 statements.

According to Matibag, the Vice President’s remarks also produced what he described as a “kinetic effect,” emboldening supporters to issue similar threats.

“The threat made by our VP has already had what is called an effect. Those who heard her threat are also imitating and making threats,” he said. “Their actions have the effect of stirring supporters to sow disorder and unrest in the country.”

Court admonition

Matibag said investigators also reviewed the affidavit of confessed Davao Death Squad member Arturo Lascañas in assessing what he described as Duterte’s “pattern of violence” during her tenure as Davao City mayor. Reading from the affidavit, he quoted Lascañas as alleging Duterte had instructed subordinates to abduct suspected criminals “so they will just go missing, and the media won’t bother us.”

Before questioning began, Escudero reminded Matibag to avoid public statements that could be interpreted as targeting members of the impeachment court.

The admonition followed Matibag’s recent public exchanges with Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano over the NBI’s decision to reopen its investigation into alleged irregularities in the country’s hosting of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games.

“I would like to remind and admonish you to avoid statements pertaining to individual members of the impeachment court,” Escudero said, adding that any dispute with the Cayetano siblings should be addressed by the Senate as a legislative body, not during the impeachment proceedings.

Neutrality challenged

Vinluan sought to undermine Matibag’s neutrality by presenting a Social Weather Stations survey showing Duterte with a 57-percent public trust rating and three opinion columns Matibag wrote for the Daily Tribune before joining the NBI: Inday Sara the Bratinella, The Bratinella is a Flat Spare Tire, and The Bratinella Sara, and Her Bad Habits.

Vinluan argued the columns reflected bias against Duterte and questioned whether they influenced the investigation.

Matibag acknowledged writing the articles but denied they affected his professional judgment, noting that the term “bratinella” originated from former President Rodrigo Duterte.

The NBI chief had served in the Duterte administration as acting Cabinet secretary, president of the National Transmission Corp. and secretary general of the Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban).

Matibag stressed that public opinion surveys do not dictate law enforcement investigations and that the bureau acts solely on evidence, law and official procedure.

Vinluan also questioned Matibag about his wife, Laguna Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Lourdes Matibag, who was among the endorsers of the impeachment complaint against Duterte, suggesting that his family had aligned itself politically against the Vice President.

Matibag maintained that the NBI’s findings were based exclusively on evidence gathered during its investigation and not on his personal views or those of his wife.

Once it concludes, House prosecutors are expected to formally rest their case on Article IV before proceeding to the second impeachment article involving the alleged misuse of confidential funds, where prosecutors are expected to present financial and audit evidence. /cb

World.title: Prosecutors: Time to put ‘fishing expedition’ argument to rest
World.content:
House prosecutor, Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno —Niño Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — For the prosecutors in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Monday’s court ruling granting their request to subpoena her tax and bank documents should already put one of the defense panel’s main arguments to rest.

Private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. and House prosecutor Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno said fishing expeditions for evidence only apply in cases where one is merely counting on the possibility that the material being sought would contain something incriminating or damaging to the accused.

‘On the off chance’

Tolosa and Diokno maintained that the prosecution had a specific set of documents in mind and knew the purpose for their production.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate okays subpoena for VP’s tax, bank docs

“We repeatedly heard the defense claiming that our request for these records was a mere fishing expedition. Although this issue should have ended because it was effectively set aside by the impeachment court after it granted our request, we just want to stress that this is not a fishing expedition,’’ Tolosa said in a media briefing.

READ: Palace agrees with decision to subpoena Sara Duterte tax, bank records

“From the start, we have identified the specific accounts that we want to see. When we say that this is a fishing expedition, this means there is no basis and you are only asking the court, for example, to look at a person’s bank accounts and hope that you accidentally spot evidence that you can use against that person,” Tolosa added.

Diokno, the House prosecutor who delivered oral arguments in support of the request, said a fishing expedition applies to a case where one seeks a subpoena “on the off chance that you find something.”

Article continues after this 

House committee hearing

Tolosa and Diokno said their request for a subpoena specifically sought bank records of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as earlier flagged by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC).

“What happened is far from a fishing expedition because we know, from the testimony and documents presented by the AMLC executive director, that the Vice President had financial transactions amounting to P6.7 billion, and we have specified the bank accounts with bank numbers, and even the branches where these involved bank accounts are located,” Tolosa said.

Article continues after this 

“Our basis (for the request) was what happened during the committee on justice hearings, especially the AMLC documents and the other witness presented regarding the allegations of unexplained wealth,” Diokno added. /cb

World.title: Groups to Cayetano: Marcoleta, Estrada not political prisoners
World.content:
Datained Senators Jinggoy Estrada (left) and Rodante Marcoleta —File photos

MANILA, Philippines — A rights group and a former political prisoner have objected to Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano referring to detained Senators Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada and former Quezon City Rep. Mike Defensor as “political prisoners.”

“We know what political persecution looks like, and the cases of these politicians and their den of thieves do not fit the definition,” Kapatid, a support group for political prisoners, said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Their detention arises from stealing millions of public and campaign funds for personal gain—serious offenses involving the abuse of public office and the betrayal of public trust,” it added.

Article continues after this 

READ: Graft court orders transfer of Marcoleta to city jail

Cayetano referred to the three politicians as political prisoners during a Facebook livestream on Friday and when he took the floor on Monday at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Marcoleta is being held on a plunder charge for failing to disclose campaign donations for his senatorial bid last year. One of the donors is Defensor, who allegedly gave P30 million.

READ: Senate enforces suspension order against Jinggoy Estrada

On the other hand, Estrada is facing plunder and graft cases over accusations that he received P573 million in kickbacks from budget allocations for flood control projects.

Article continues after this 

‘False prophets’

According to Kapatid, many of the country’s estimated 675 political prisoners come from marginalized communities and have faced Red-tagging, fabricated charges, planted evidence and prolonged detention.

It said the term political prisoner should be reserved for those deprived of liberty for asserting their fundamental rights and advocating for social justice.

Article continues after this 

These individuals chose “a path defined not by self-interest but by selflessness, sacrifice, and a commitment to the collective good,” the group added.

“Words can easily be weaponized by false prophets. To describe those charged with corruption as ‘political prisoners’ distorts both law and history,” Kapatid said.

It cited the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe Resolution 1900 (2012) which defines a political prisoner as an individual whose detention stems from politically driven state actions or from exercising fundamental freedoms, including expression, assembly and association.

“The defining characteristic of political imprisonment is political persecution. In these cases, the state routinely fabricates or manipulates criminal charges against dissidents and activists to hide the purely political nature of their arrest,” Kapatid said.

In a statement by human rights group Karapatan, former political prisoner Amanda Echanis called Cayetano’s words a “grave insult to the 560 political prisoners and scores of former political prisoners.”

‘Grave insult’

“Excuse me, Senator Cayetano, but plunderers cannot be considered as such because they are simply crooks in authority and mercenaries of their political patrons,” said Echanis who is also the spokesperson for LAYA, a campaign to free all political prisoners.

“They steal from public funds, live in luxury at the behest of the people’s poverty, and when made accountable for their crimes, they use their political capital to affirm the double standard of justice in the country,” she added.

Recalling her own experience, Echanis said she was arrested during the Duterte administration while working as a peasant organizer and caring for her infant child.

World.title: ‘Main chunk’ of impeach court’s ruling on subpoenas prepared in advance
World.content:
There will be only one trial day in Week 4 of the Sara Duterte impeachment proceedings. —Inquirer photo/Niño Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — The major points of the Senate impeachment court’s decision allowing the issuance of a subpoena for Vice President Sara Duterte’s tax and bank records had already been prepared before the trial proper started on July 6.

This was according to the court’s spokesperson, Regie Tongol, as he disclosed what went behind Monday’s ruling delivered in open court by the presiding officer, Sen. Francis Escudero, which granted the House prosecutors’ request to subpoena confidential documents that they said would support the charge that Duterte amassed ill-gotten wealth while in office.

“So basically the main chunk of the decision of the presiding officer has already been prepared even before July 6th,” Tongol said in a media briefing ahead of the resumption of the trial on Tuesday.

Article continues after this 

READ: Group hails subpoena for Sara Duterte’s bank, tax records

“So I think the presiding officer also, during the caucus, consulted his fellow senator-judges about it and asked about their views regarding the matter and that is the request of the other senator-judges to study it until the weekend and until today. So, handa na naman siya (it has been prepared) ever since,” he added.

Tongol noted that the request for the subpoenas was already stated in the pretrial briefs presented by the prosecution panel and was just renewed during the trial.

READ: VP’s lawyers shocked, respects prepared ruling on financial, tax records

Prior to Escudero reading out the ruling, the senator-judges were expected to vote on the matter in open session, given the strong objections raised by the defense.

Article continues after this 

The defense team’s spokesperson, Michael Poa, said he was surprised to learn that most parts of the ruling read by Escudero were already finished even before the trial began.

But Poa said he and his felllow counsels would respect the ruling.

Article continues after this 

“Actually, I was surprised too when I read it,” said Poa at a press conference.

“But nonetheless, I don’t really want to read too much into it. I don’t want to cast aspersions on what happened yesterday,” he said.

Poa said it was possible that the senator-judges had already come up with their respective positions but still allowed both sides to deliver oral arguments on Monday to see if they could still change the resolution.

World.title: Astana Unveils Competition Schedule for Games of Future 2026
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Tourism and Sports has released the competition schedule for the international Phygital Games of the Future 2026, scheduled for July 29-Aug. 9, bringing together athletes and gamers in competitions that combine physical and digital disciplines.

The tournament will open with the 3on3 Freestyle phygital basketball event on July 29, followed by the PUBG competition from July 31 to Aug. 2. DOTA 2 (MOBA PC) matches are scheduled for Aug. 2-5, while the Counter-Strike phygital shooter tournament will run from Aug. 4-8. The UFL phygital football competition will take place on Aug. 4-9.

The Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MOBA Mobile) tournament is set for Aug. 6-9, alongside the Just Dance phygital dancing competition on Aug. 6-7. The tournament will conclude with the Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves phygital fighting event on Aug. 8.

The tournament is expected to welcome more than 800 participants representing over 50 nationalities, united in international clubs. It will also bring together technology brands and thousands of spectators for 12 days of competitions combining digital and physical sports.

World.title: Shanghai and Technology Turn in Kazakhstan-China Relations
World.content:
Kazakhstan’s largest Chinese business round in years put data, computing and digital logistics at the center. The measure of it will be deployment.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s working visit to Shanghai on July 16-17 produced a familiar number and a new emphasis. Kazakhstan and China signed more than 70 commercial documents worth over $15 billion, covering artificial intelligence, transport, finance, agriculture and machinery. What set this round apart was where the weight fell. The center of gravity sat in data, computing and digital logistics, the fields that will define the next decade of the relationship, rather than in the oil, metals and transit flows that built it.

Tokayev opened the roundtable with the figures that anchor the partnership and a phrase to frame them. The two countries, he said, have entered a new “golden thirty years.” Bilateral trade reached $49 billion in 2025, a record, and Chinese firms have put more than $30 billion into the Kazakh economy, with over 8,500 enterprises carrying Chinese capital now active in the country. He named CNPC, CITIC and Huawei among the anchors, then pointed to a newer industrial layer: a gas chemical complex with Sinopec, a corn processing plant with Fufeng and a textile cluster with Lihua, alongside multi-brand vehicle assembly for Changan, Great Wall Motor and Chery. The value of Chinese participation, in his telling, sits increasingly in jobs, technology and industrial depth, with raw trade volume the older part of the story.

The pivot to data and computing

The signing list showed the shift in plain terms. Huawei took the largest share, concluding a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development and a separate equipment supply agreement with Samruk-Kazyna. Kazakhtelecom signed a framework with Hengtong Group on Data Center Valley, the gigawatt-scale computing complex rising near Ekibastuz. Almaty gained an artificial intelligence and robotics agreement involving UBTECH, and Kazakh universities tied up with Shanghai and Suzhou institutions. The timing was deliberate. The visit opened alongside the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, where Astana joined 29 governments in the Shanghai-based World AI Cooperation Organization.

Data Center Valley is where Kazakhstan’s positioning becomes legible. The same Ekibastuz site that now draws Chinese fibre and construction capital also anchors a $10 billion arrangement with Nvidia and a US-linked cloud partner, reported earlier this summer. Astana is not committing to one technology ecosystem. It is inviting both and pricing the same underlying assets into each: land, spare grid capacity and electricity near $0.025 per kilowatt-hour. Power that is scarce and expensive in the United States and Europe is abundant and cheap in northern Kazakhstan, and the government is monetizing that gap across the very rivalry that constrains hyperscale expansion elsewhere.

Mobility and ports rounded out the industrial side. Allur signed to build Li Auto vehicles in Kazakhstan, Astana Motors licensed Omoda and Jaecoo assembly with Chery, and Samruk-Kazyna, Freedom Holding and Astana’s city administration agreed a framework with Geely on electric-vehicle charging and automotive AI. On the Caspian, Guoyou committed to a multifunctional terminal at Kuryk, the port that feeds Kazakh cargo onto the Trans-Caspian route. In parallel talks, Tokayev discussed a first Central Asian battery plant with CATL. Each of these keeps more of the manufacturing chain inside the country.

Corridors, minerals and the deployment question

The logistics agenda followed the same logic. About 85% of China-Europe rail traffic already crosses Kazakhstan, and freight with China rose roughly 9% in the first half of 2026 to 18.7 million tons, while container trains dispatched from China through the country climbed more than a third year on year. In Shanghai, Tokayev sold the next layer, a digital one: Smart Cargo, a single window pooling customs, logistics and commercial data, built so that goods clear borders at something closer to the speed at which data moves. The framing matters because the Middle Corridor’s physical ceiling is fixed. Two changes of rail gauge and a Caspian crossing keep it structurally more expensive than the all-water route to Europe. Additional value has to come from speed, transparency and digital integration, since the geography will not yield maritime-scale tonnage.

Critical minerals formed the other pillar. Tokayev restated the demand Kazakhstan now makes of every partner it courts, which is processing and manufacturing capacity on Kazakh soil, with extraction rights as the opening term rather than the prize. That message runs alongside Astana’s parallel engagement with Washington and Brussels on rare earth separation and refining. It is also the message the Shanghai deals encode. The stated goal across them is technology transfer, research centres and production chains, with capital treated as the entry ticket.

The authors are Alexander Dergay, a column writer for Berliner Zeitung and the Ostdeutsche Allgemeine, and Eldaniz Gusseinov, a co-founder and head of research at Nightingale Int.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Austria Deepen Strategic Ties with New Connectivity Platform
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan and Austria officially launched the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform at the Austrian Parliament on July 15 to strengthen bilateral cooperation in transport, logistics, infrastructure, energy and investment, reported the Austrian Press Agency.

The platform aims to bring together government agencies, businesses and financial institutions from both countries to develop joint projects and improve transport connectivity between Europe and Central Asia.

The launch reflects the growing economic and political partnership between Kazakhstan and Austria, which have expanded cooperation in recent years through closer political dialogue and increasing trade and investment ties.

“Austria is home to highly competitive companies, advanced industrial expertise and a strong culture of innovation. Kazakhstan, in turn, offers considerable economic potential and is emerging as one of Central Asia’s key economic partners. Our role is to bring companies together and help turn business opportunities into lasting partnerships. The strong response to our inaugural event shows there is clear demand for a platform that can do exactly that,” said Karl Jurka, president of the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform.

President of the Austrian National Council Walter Rosenkranz welcomed the initiative, describing it as an effective mechanism for advancing cooperation in transport, logistics, sustainable infrastructure, digitalization and energy. He also highlighted the potential for further expanding bilateral relations.

The Kazakh Ambassador to Austria Mukhtar Tileuberdi said strengthening transport connectivity remains one of Kazakhstan’s strategic priorities. He presented the country’s efforts to further develop the Middle Corridor, a key trade route linking Europe and Asia.

Tileuberdi also briefed participants on Kazakhstan’s domestic reforms, noting that the country’s new Constitution entered into force on July 1 following its approval in a nationwide referendum. According to him, the updated Constitution expands Parliament’s powers, strengthens protections for citizens’ rights and freedoms, increases government accountability and further improves the investment climate.

He said the reforms initiated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev are aimed at building a Just Kazakhstan based on the rule of law, openness and sustainable development.

Alexander Schierhuber, Kazakhstan’s honorary consul in Lower Austria and vice president of the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform, noted that the initiative is intended to serve as a bridge between the two economies by providing businesses with a trusted platform for networking, dialogue and long-term cooperation.

“At a time of geopolitical change and evolving trade routes, reliable frameworks that allow companies to engage directly with one another are becoming increasingly important,” he said.

The launch marks a new step in Kazakh-Austrian relations, reinforcing both countries’ commitment to expanding strategic cooperation and promoting sustainable transport links between Europe and Central Asia.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Produce Li Auto, Omoda, Jaecoo Vehicles, Autonomous Trucks by 2028
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan plans to launch production of Li Auto, Omoda, and Jaecoo vehicles by 2028 as part of a broader effort to expand its automotive industry, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and introduce advanced technologies, Minister of Industry and Construction Yersayin Nagaspayev said at a July 21 government meeting.

The initiative follows agreements reached during President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s recent state visit to China. In addition to passenger vehicle production, Kazakhstan will manufacture autonomous SITRAK semi-trailer tractors and cooperate with BYD to develop a nationwide network of high-speed charging stations for electric vehicles.

The country is also expanding commercial vehicle manufacturing. Hyundai Trans Auto is scheduled to begin producing 500 Volvo semi-trailer tractors annually starting in the fourth quarter of this year, while Barys Truck Manufactory, in partnership with China’s XCMG, will launch production of electric heavy-duty trucks, reported Kazinform.

Nagaspayev said automotive manufacturers are integrating artificial intelligence and digital technologies in line with the President’s instructions. An AI-powered situational center has already been commissioned to improve operational safety by analyzing data from surveillance cameras, sensors, and other information systems to detect risks and emergencies in real time.

Kazakhstan currently has 11 enterprises producing passenger cars, buses, trucks, and specialized vehicles. Last year, the country commissioned the KIA Qazaqstan and Astana Motors Manufacturing Kazakhstan plants, with combined investment exceeding 346 billion tenge (US$735 million).

World.title: UNESCO Committee Reviews Kazakhstan’s Bid to List Mangystau Rock Mosques as World Heritage
World.content:
ASTANA – The UNESCO World Heritage Committee has begun reviewing Kazakhstan’s nomination of the Rock Mosques of Mangystau and Associated Sacred Sites for inscription on the World Heritage List during its 48th session in Busan, South Korea.

The 48th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee opened on July 19 in Busan and will run through July 29, bringing together around 3,000 delegates from the 196 States Parties to the World Heritage Convention, along with representatives of international organizations and heritage experts, reported the Kazakh Foreign Ministry’s press service on July 20.

The committee will consider 30 new nominations for inscription on the UNESCO World Heritage List and review 147 State of Conservation reports on properties already inscribed.

Kazakhstan is participating in the session as a member of the World Heritage Committee. Among the nominations under consideration is The Rock Mosques of Mangystau and Associated Sacred Sites.

According to State Counselor Erlan Karin, the nomination follows President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s instruction at the 2024 National Kurultai in Atyrau to begin the process of seeking UNESCO World Heritage status for Mangystau’s unique underground mosques.

Karin said extensive work has since been completed to prepare the nomination dossier, including scientific research and legal and institutional documentation. An evaluation mission visited Kazakhstan last year, and the country has recently received a technical assessment from the UNESCO World Heritage Center and the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS).

A decision on the nomination is expected during the current committee session and is regarded as a significant milestone for Kazakhstan’s cultural heritage preservation efforts.

World.title: China Eastern Plans Direct Astana-Shanghai Flights, FlyArystan Adds Chongqing Route
World.content:
ASTANA — Kazakhstan is set to expand its air connectivity with China as China Eastern Airlines plans to launch direct flights between Astana and Shanghai this autumn, while FlyArystan will open a new route between Almaty and Chongqing in September.

Chair of the Civil Aviation Committee of Kazakhstan’s Transport Ministry Saltanat Tompiyeva met with China Eastern Airlines Senior Vice President for Marketing and Sales Jin Chenhua during a working visit to China, reported the ministry’s press service on July 20.

The officials discussed the launch of direct Astana-Shanghai flights. The airline confirmed strong commercial interest in the route and said it plans to begin operations this autumn after completing the necessary preparations.

The service will initially operate three times a week, with plans to increase frequency to daily flights.

The meeting also covered opportunities to expand air links between Kazakhstan and China. China Eastern expressed interest in increasing the number of flights to Kazakhstan and strengthening cooperation with Kazakh airlines.

China Eastern Airlines is one of China’s three largest state-owned carriers and the country’s second-largest airline. Based in Shanghai, it operates a fleet of 834 aircraft and carried around 150 million passengers in 2025.

FlyArystan launches Chongqing route

Also, low-cost carrier FlyArystan announced the launch of a new international route between Almaty and Chongqing.

The inaugural flight is scheduled for Sept. 23, with services operating twice a week. Flights will depart Almaty on Wednesdays and Saturdays, with return flights from Chongqing on Thursdays and Sundays.

The new service will become FlyArystan’s fifth destination in China, complementing its existing routes to Urumqi, Yining (Kulja) and Xi’an.

The flight time between Almaty and Chongqing will be approximately five hours.

World.title: Kazakhstan Holds Off Global Fertility Decline, For Now
World.content:
ASTANA – As fertility rates continue to fall across much of the world, Kazakhstan is among the countries where births are still above the population replacement level. New data, however, indicate that the country is beginning to mirror the broader global demographic slowdown.

According to the United Nations, the global fertility rate has dropped from around five children per woman half a century ago to roughly 2.2 today, reshaping population structures and creating long-term economic and social challenges for many countries. Much of Europe and East Asia has fallen well below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman.

Kazakhstan, however, remains above that threshold at 2.57. A continuous belt of countries stretching from Pakistan to Mongolia still records fertility above the replacement level, and Kazakhstan is part of that group.

According to the Bureau of National Statistics, the country’s population has reached 20.58 million, an increase of more than 76,000 since the start of 2026.

Kazakhstan remains a regional demographic leader

Kazakhstan continues to rank among the region’s demographic leaders. According to available estimates, Uzbekistan records one of the region’s highest fertility rates at around 3.45 children per woman, while the Kyrgyz Republic stands at 2.75. Kazakhstan, at 2.57, remains well above Russia’s 1.46, Armenia’s 1.71, and Belarus’s roughly 1.2.

At the same time, birth numbers in Kazakhstan have started to decline from the unusually high levels recorded during and immediately after the COVID-19 period. According to an analysis by Finprom.kz, 74,100 children were born in Kazakhstan in the first quarter of 2026, down from 77,300 in the same period last year, a decline of 4.2%, or around 3,200 fewer births.

The decline affected both urban and rural areas, though it was sharper in the countryside. Urban births fell by 2.3%, from 46,700 to 45,600, while rural births dropped by 7.2%, from 30,700 to 28,500. No major gender imbalance was recorded. In the first quarter of 2026, 38,000 boys and 36,100 girls were born, compared with 39,600 boys and 37,700 girls a year earlier.

Regionally, the largest number of births was recorded in the Turkistan Region with 10,400 newborns, followed by Almaty city with 7,200, Shymkent city with 6,300, and the Almaty Region and Astana city with 6,200 each. The lowest totals were in the Ulytau Region with 738 births, the North Kazakhstan Region with 1,100, the East Kazakhstan Region with 1,600, and the Abai and Kostanai regions with 1,800 each.

Part of a broader global shift

Experts say Kazakhstan’s recent decline should not be viewed as a demographic crisis, but rather as part of the so-called second demographic transition seen in many countries as education levels rise, urbanization accelerates, women’s labor force participation expands, and the cost of raising children increases.

For years, Kazakhstan stood out from that global pattern by maintaining comparatively high fertility even as many countries saw sustained declines.

According to Aslan Temirkhanov, a medical doctor, specialist in molecular medicine and cell biology, and expert in youth reproductive health, the current decline is not critical and should be interpreted in context.

“We know that during the COVID-19 period, many countries saw a temporary spike in births because people were staying at home and their lifestyles changed. What we are seeing now is partly an adjustment after that peak,” Temirkhanov told The Astana Times.

In other words, Kazakhstan’s recent decline may say less about a sudden demographic breakdown than about normalization after an exceptional period. The more important measure, he suggests, is not the quarterly number of births alone but the country’s broader fertility trajectory over time.

“If we look not just at the absolute number of births but at broader demographic indicators, Kazakhstan still has a high fertility rate. In Russia, for example, the fertility rate is around 1.3. In the European Union it is roughly 1.5. In South Korea it is below 0.8,” he said.

Temirkhanov noted that economic uncertainty is one of the factors shaping reproductive decisions worldwide. In cities, especially Astana and Almaty, the cost of housing, childcare and everyday life can encourage couples to postpone having children or to have fewer children than earlier generations. Women’s educational attainment and labor force participation have also risen, which is generally associated with later family formation and smaller family size unless strong family support policies are in place.

However, that does not mean Kazakhstan is destined to follow the same path as East Asia or southern Europe. But it does suggest that the country’s demographic future will depend increasingly on how well it manages the social and economic conditions surrounding family life.

Education and healthcare as demographic investments

Temirkhanov said Kazakhstan’s relatively strong fertility rate reflects a combination of factors, including state support for families, cultural norms and the availability of reproductive health education and services. He also pointed to cultural expectations around family, but emphasized that one of the most important factors is comprehensive sexuality education.

“Education affects the quality of family planning, knowledge about contraception, understanding when to see a doctor and awareness of reproductive health services,” he said.

According to Temirkhanov, many young people in Kazakhstan are still unaware that the country has youth health centers offering free counseling and services related to reproductive and mental health.

Kazakhstan has more than 100 youth health centers that provide medical, preventive, psychosocial and legal services to adolescents ages 10 to 18 and young adults ages 18 to 29 on issues related to reproductive and mental health. He cited a 2025 UNFPA study on adolescents and youth ages 15-19 and 20-24, which found low levels of reproductive health knowledge. According to the report, only 11.7% of respondents demonstrated awareness of HIV, including 8.1% of adolescents ages 15-19 and 19.1% of young people ages 20-24.

“Awareness of sexually transmitted infections and their consequences, including infertility if left untreated, was also low.
